sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第209巻

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 209
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 209

sentences.zh: 【唐紀二十五】 起著雍涒灘，盡上章閹茂七月，凡二年有奇。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 25] From Zhuanyou Cuotan through the seventh month of Shangzhang Yanmao; a little more than two years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 25] From Zhuanyou Cuotan through the seventh month of Shangzhang Yanmao—slightly more than two years in all.

sentences.zh: 春，二月，庚寅，宮有言皇后衣笥裙上有五色雲起，上令圖以示百官。

translations.literal: In spring, the second month, on gengyin, someone in the palace reported that five-colored clouds had risen on the empress's skirt in her clothes chest; the emperor ordered it painted and shown to the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the second month, on gengyin, palace insiders reported that five-colored clouds had appeared on the empress's skirt in her wardrobe chest. The emperor had the scene painted and displayed to the entire court.

sentences.zh: 韋巨源請布之天下；

translations.literal: Wei Juyuan requested that it be proclaimed throughout the realm;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Juyuan asked that the omen be announced throughout the realm;

sentences.zh: 從之，乃赦天下。

translations.literal: the emperor assented, and thereupon proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor agreed, and a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 迦葉志忠奏：「昔神堯皇帝未受命，天下歌《桃李子》；

translations.literal: Jaye Zhizhong memorialized: "In former times, before Divine Yao Emperor received the Mandate, the realm sang 'Peach and Plum';
translations.idiomatic: Jaye Zhizhong submitted a memorial: "In former times, before Emperor Gaozu received the Mandate, the realm sang 'Peach and Plum';

sentences.zh: 文武皇帝未受命，天下歌《秦王破陣樂》；

translations.literal: before Civil and Martial Emperor received the Mandate, the realm sang 'Prince of Qin Smashes the Battle Array';
translations.idiomatic: before Emperor Taizong received the Mandate, the realm sang 'Prince of Qin Smashes the Battle Array';

sentences.zh: 天皇大帝未受命，天下歌《堂堂》；

translations.literal: before Heavenly Sovereign Great Emperor received the Mandate, the realm sang 'Stately and Grand';
translations.idiomatic: before Emperor Gaozong received the Mandate, the realm sang 'Stately and Grand';

sentences.zh: 則天皇后未受命，天下歌《嫵媚娘》；

translations.literal: before Empress Zetian received the Mandate, the realm sang 'Charming Lady';
translations.idiomatic: before Empress Wu Zetian received the Mandate, the realm sang 'Charming Lady';

sentences.zh: 應天皇帝未受命，天下歌《英王石州》。

translations.literal: before Responding-to-Heaven Emperor received the Mandate, the realm sang 'Prince of Ying's Shizhou.'
translations.idiomatic: before Emperor Ruizong received the Mandate, the realm sang 'Prince of Ying's Shizhou.'

sentences.zh: 順天皇后未受命，天下歌《桑條韋》，蓋天意以爲順天皇后宜爲國母，主蠶桑之事。

translations.literal: Before Empress Shuntian received the Mandate, the realm sang 'Mulberry Branch and Wei'—Heaven's intent, it seems, was that Empress Shuntian should be mother of the state and preside over sericulture.
translations.idiomatic: Before the empress received the Mandate, the realm sang 'Mulberry Branch and Wei'—Heaven's intent, it seems, was that she should be mother of the state and oversee sericulture.

sentences.zh: 謹上《桑韋歌》十二篇，請編之樂府，皇后祀先蠶則奏之。」

translations.literal: I respectfully present twelve pieces of the 'Mulberry and Wei Songs' and request that they be compiled in the Music Bureau and performed when the empress sacrifices to the Silkworm Ancestress."
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully present twelve pieces of the 'Mulberry and Wei Songs' and ask that they be entered in the Music Bureau and performed when the empress sacrifices to the Silkworm Ancestress."

sentences.zh: 太常卿鄭愔又引而申之。

translations.literal: The Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Zheng Yin, further cited and elaborated on this.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Zheng Yin, further cited and elaborated on the argument.

sentences.zh: 上悅，皆受厚賞。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased, and all received generous rewards.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased, and all were richly rewarded.

sentences.zh: 右補闕趙延禧上言：「周、唐一統，符命同歸，故髙宗封陛下爲周王；

translations.literal: Right Remonstrance Archivist Zhao Yanxi submitted: "Zhou and Tang were unified in one rule, and their portents and mandates converged on the same end—therefore Emperor Gaozong enfeoffed Your Majesty as Prince of Zhou;
translations.idiomatic: Right Remonstrance Archivist Zhao Yanxi submitted: "Zhou and Tang were united under one rule, and their portents and mandates converged on the same end—therefore Emperor Gaozong enfeoffed Your Majesty as Prince of Zhou;

sentences.zh: 則天時，唐同泰獻《洛水圖》。

translations.literal: in Empress Wu's time, Tang Tongtai presented the 'Chart of the Luo River.'
translations.idiomatic: in Empress Wu's time, Tang Tongtai presented the 'Chart of the Luo River.'

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：『其或繼周者，雖百代可知也。』

translations.literal: Confucius said: 'Whoever may succeed Zhou—even a hundred generations hence may be known.'
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: 'Whoever may succeed Zhou—even a hundred generations hence may be known.'

sentences.zh: 陛下繼則天，子孫當百代王天下。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty succeeds Empress Wu; your descendants should rule All-under-Heaven for a hundred generations."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty succeeds Empress Wu; your descendants should rule All-under-Heaven for a hundred generations."

sentences.zh: 上悅，擢延禧爲諫議大夫。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and promoted Yanxi to Remonstrance and Discussion Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and promoted Yanxi to Remonstrance and Discussion Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，蕭至忠上疎，以爲：「恩幸者止可富之金帛，食之梁肉，不可以公器爲私用。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Xiao Zhizhong submitted a memorial, stating: "Favored intimates should only be enriched with gold and silks and fed with fine grain and meat; public instruments must not be used for private ends.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Xiao Zhizhong submitted a memorial, stating: "Favored intimates should only be enriched with gold and silks and fed with fine grain and meat; public office must not be turned to private use.

sentences.zh: 今列位已廣，冗員倍之，干求未厭，日月增數。

translations.literal: Now the roster of offices is already broad, and supernumeraries double it; importunate requests are never satisfied, and their number grows day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Now the roster of offices is already broad, and supernumeraries double it; importunate requests are never satisfied, and their number grows day by day.

sentences.zh: 陛下降不貲之澤，近戚有無涯之請，賣官利己，鬻法徇私。

translations.literal: Your Majesty bestows inexhaustible bounty, while close kin have boundless petitions; offices are sold for private gain and laws peddled for personal favor.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty bestows inexhaustible bounty, while close kin have boundless petitions; offices are sold for private gain and laws peddled for personal favor.

sentences.zh: 台寺之内，朱紫盈滿，忽事則不存職務，恃勢則公違憲章，徒忝官曹，無益時政。」

translations.literal: Within the censorial and ministerial halls, red and purple robes fill every seat; when nothing is afoot they neglect their duties, and when they rely on influence they openly violate statutes—they merely disgrace their offices and do no good for current policy."
translations.idiomatic: Within the censorial and ministerial halls, red and purple robes fill every seat; when nothing is afoot they neglect their duties, and when they rely on influence they openly violate the law— they merely disgrace their offices and do nothing for the governance of the day."

sentences.zh: 上雖嘉其意，竟不能用。

translations.literal: Although the emperor approved of his intent, in the end he could not put it into practice.
translations.idiomatic: Although the emperor approved of his intent, in the end he could not act on it.

sentences.zh: 三月，丙辰，朔方道大總管張仁願築三受降城於河上。

translations.literal: In the third month, on bingchen, Zhang Rengui, Grand General of the Shuofang Circuit, built three Cities to Receive Surrender on the river.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on bingchen, Zhang Rengui, Grand General of the Shuofang Circuit, built three Cities to Receive Surrender on the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 初，朔方軍與突厥以河爲境，河北有拂雲祠，突厥將入寇，必先詣祠祈禱，牧馬料兵而後度河。

translations.literal: Initially, the Shuofang army and the Turks took the river as their border; north of the river stood the Fuyun Shrine. When the Turks were about to raid, they always first went to the shrine to pray, pastured their horses and counted their troops, and only then crossed the river.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, the Shuofang army and the Turks took the river as their border; north of the river stood the Fuyun Shrine. When the Turks were about to raid, they always first went to the shrine to pray, pastured their horses and mustered their troops, and only then crossed the river.

sentences.zh: 時默啜悉衆西撃突騎施，仁願請乘虚奪取漠南地，於河北築三受降城，首尾相應，以絶其南寇之路。

translations.literal: At this time Mokchuo had led all his forces west to attack the Qarlugs; Rengui requested to seize the vacant moment, take the lands south of the desert, and build three Cities to Receive Surrender north of the river, linked head to tail, to cut off their southern raiding route.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Mokchuo had led all his forces west to attack the Qarlugs; Rengui asked to seize the moment, take the lands south of the desert, and build three Cities to Receive Surrender north of the river, linked head to tail, to cut off their southern raiding route.

sentences.zh: 太子少師唐休璟以爲：「兩漢以來皆北阻大河，今築城寇境，恐勞人費功，終爲虜有。」

translations.literal: Taizi Shaoshi Tang Xiujing held that: "Since the two Han dynasties, all have relied on the great river as a northern barrier; now to build cities in the enemy's territory will, I fear, weary the people and waste effort, and in the end they will fall to the barbarians."
translations.idiomatic: Taizi Shaoshi Tang Xiujing argued: "Since the two Han dynasties, all have relied on the great river as a northern barrier; now to build cities in enemy territory will, I fear, weary the people and waste effort, and in the end they will fall to the barbarians."

sentences.zh: 仁願固請不已，上竟從之。

translations.literal: Rengui pressed his request without cease, and the emperor at last assented.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui pressed his request without cease, and the emperor at last assented.

sentences.zh: 仁願表留歳滿鎭兵以助其功，咸陽兵二百餘人逃歸，仁願悉擒之，斬於城下，軍中股慄，六旬而成。

translations.literal: Rengui memorialized to retain troops whose garrison terms had expired to assist the work; more than two hundred soldiers from Xianyang fled home, and Rengui seized them all and beheaded them below the wall. The army trembled in its legs, and the work was completed in sixty days.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui memorialized to retain troops whose garrison terms had expired to assist the work; more than two hundred soldiers from Xianyang fled home, and Rengui seized them all and beheaded them below the wall. The army trembled with fear, and the work was completed in sixty days.

sentences.zh: 以拂雲祠爲中城，距東西兩城各四百餘里，皆據津要，拓地三百餘里。

translations.literal: The Fuyun Shrine served as the middle city; east and west cities lay more than four hundred li apart, each holding a strategic crossing, and the territory was extended more than three hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: The Fuyun Shrine served as the middle city; the eastern and western cities lay more than four hundred li apart, each holding a strategic crossing, and the territory was extended more than three hundred li.

sentences.zh: 於牛頭朝那山北，置烽候千八百所，以左玉鈐衞將軍論弓仁爲朔方軍前鋒游弈使，戍諾眞水爲邏衞。

translations.literal: North of Niutou Chaona Mountain, eighteen hundred beacon stations were set up; Lun Gongren, General of the Left Jade Bell Guard, was made Vanguard Patrol Commissioner of the Shuofang army and garrisoned at Nuozhen River as border guard.
translations.idiomatic: North of Niutou Chaona Mountain, eighteen hundred beacon stations were set up; Lun Gongren, General of the Left Jade Bell Guard, was made Vanguard Patrol Commissioner of the Shuofang army and garrisoned at Nuozhen River as border guard.

sentences.zh: 自是突厥不敢度山畋牧，朔方無復寇掠，減鎭兵數萬人。

translations.literal: From this time the Turks did not dare cross the mountains to hunt or pasture; Shuofang knew no further raids, and several tens of thousands of garrison troops were reduced.
translations.idiomatic: From this time the Turks did not dare cross the mountains to hunt or pasture; Shuofang knew no further raids, and several tens of thousands of garrison troops were reduced.

sentences.zh: 仁願建三城，不置壅門及備守之具。

translations.literal: When Rengui built the three cities, he did not install barrier gates or defensive equipment.
translations.idiomatic: When Rengui built the three cities, he did not install barrier gates or defensive equipment.

sentences.zh: 或問之，仁願曰：「兵貴進取，不利退守。

translations.literal: When someone questioned this, Rengui said: "Soldiers value advancing and taking the offensive; retreat and defense are not to their advantage.
translations.idiomatic: When someone questioned this, Rengui said: "Soldiers value advancing and taking the offensive; retreat and defense are not to their advantage.

sentences.zh: 寇至此，當並力出戰，回首望城者，猶應斬之，安用守備，生其退恧之心也！」

translations.literal: When the enemy comes here, we should unite our strength and go out to fight; even one who looks back toward the city should still be beheaded—what use are defenses that breed a mind of retreat and shame!"
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy comes here, we should unite our strength and go out to fight; even one who looks back toward the city should still be beheaded—what use are defenses that breed a mind of retreat and shame!"

sentences.zh: 其後常元楷爲朔方軍總管，始築壅門。

translations.literal: Later, when Chang Yuankai became Commander of the Shuofang army, he first built barrier gates.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Chang Yuankai became Commander of the Shuofang army, he first built barrier gates.

sentences.zh: 人以是重仁願而輕元楷。

translations.literal: People therefore esteemed Rengui and looked down on Yuankai.
translations.idiomatic: People therefore esteemed Rengui and looked down on Yuankai.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，癸未，置修文館大學士四員，直學士八員，學士十二員，選公卿以下善爲文者李嶠等爲之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on guiwei, four Grand Academicians of the Xiuxuan Hall, eight Direct Academicians, and twelve Academicians were appointed; Li Qiao and others, chosen from among dukes, ministers, and below who excelled in letters, were made such.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on guiwei, four Grand Academicians of the Xiuxuan Hall, eight Direct Academicians, and twelve Academicians were appointed; Li Qiao and others, chosen from among dukes, ministers, and below who excelled in letters, were made such.

sentences.zh: 毎游幸禁苑，或宗戚宴集，學士無不畢從，賦詩屬和，使上官昭容第其甲乙，優者賜金帛；

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor toured the forbidden park or kinsmen gathered for banquets, the academicians all attended without exception, composing and matching poems; Shangguan Zhaorong ranked them in grades, and the superior received gold and silks;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor toured the forbidden park or kinsmen gathered for banquets, the academicians all attended without exception, composing and matching poems; Shangguan Zhaorong ranked them in grades, and the superior received gold and silks;

sentences.zh: 同預宴者，惟中書、門下及長參王公、親貴數人而已，至大宴，方召八座、九列、諸司五品以上預焉。

translations.literal: those who shared the banquet were only a few from the Secretariat and Chancellery, senior-attending princes and dukes, and close nobles; only at great banquets were the eight chief ministers, the nine ranks, and officials of the fifth grade and above from the various bureaus summoned.
translations.idiomatic: those who shared the banquet were only a few from the Secretariat and Chancellery, senior-attending princes and dukes, and close nobles; only at great banquets were the eight chief ministers, the nine ranks, and officials of the fifth grade and above from the various bureaus summoned.

sentences.zh: 於是天下靡然，爭以文華相尚，儒學中讜之士莫得進矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon all under Heaven turned to it, each vying to esteem literary ornament; upright scholars of Confucian learning could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon all under Heaven turned to it, each vying to esteem literary ornament; upright scholars of Confucian learning could not advance.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，癸巳，以左屯衞大將軍、朔方道大總管張仁願同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on guisi, Zhang Rengui, General-in-Chief of the Left Tunwei Guard and Grand General of the Shuofang Circuit, was made of equal rank with the three offices of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on guisi, Zhang Rengui, General-in-Chief of the Left Tunwei Guard and Grand General of the Shuofang Circuit, was made of equal rank with the three offices of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 甲午，淸源尉呂元泰上疎，以爲：「邊境未寧，鎭戍不息，士卒困苦，轉輸疲弊，而營建佛寺，月廣歳滋，勞人費財，無有窮極。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Lü Yuantai, Commandant of Qingyuan, submitted a memorial, stating: "The borders are not yet tranquil, garrisons never cease, soldiers suffer hardship, and transport and supply are worn out—yet Buddhist temples are built, growing month by month and year by year, wearying the people and wasting wealth without limit.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Lü Yuantai, Commandant of Qingyuan, submitted a memorial, stating: "The borders are not yet tranquil, garrisons never cease, soldiers suffer hardship, and transport and supply are worn out—yet Buddhist temples are built, growing month by month and year by year, wearying the people and wasting wealth without limit.

sentences.zh: 昔黃帝、堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武惟以儉約仁義立德垂名，晉、宋以降，塔廟競起，而喪亂相繼，由其好尚失所，奢靡相髙，人不堪命故也。

translations.literal: In former times Huangdi, Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu established virtue and left their names solely through frugality, restraint, benevolence, and righteousness; from Jin and Song onward, pagodas and temples vied to rise, yet disorder and ruin followed in succession—because their cherished pursuits lost their proper place, extravagance vied in height, and the people could not bear the burden of command.
translations.idiomatic: In former times Huangdi, Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu established virtue and left their names solely through frugality, restraint, benevolence, and righteousness; from Jin and Song onward, pagodas and temples vied to rise, yet disorder and ruin followed in succession—because their cherished pursuits lost their proper place, extravagance vied in height, and the people could not bear the burden of command.

sentences.zh: 伏願回營造之資，充疆塲之費，使烽燧永息，群生富庶，則如來慈悲之施，平等之心，孰過於此？」

translations.literal: I humbly wish that funds for construction be turned to expenses for the frontier, that beacon fires cease forever and the multitude grow rich—then what could surpass this as the Tathagata's compassionate gift and mind of equality?"
translations.idiomatic: I humbly wish that funds for construction be turned to expenses for the frontier, that beacon fires cease forever and the multitude grow rich—then what could surpass this as the Tathagata's compassionate gift and mind of equality?"

sentences.zh: 疎奏，不省。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted, but the emperor took no notice.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted, but the emperor took no notice.

sentences.zh: 安樂、長寧公主及皇后妹成國夫人、上官婕妤、婕妤母沛國夫人鄭氏、尚宮柴氏、賀婁氏、女巫第五英兒、隴西夫人趙氏，皆依勢用事，請謁受賕，雖屠沽臧獲，用錢三十萬，則別降墨敕除官，斜封付中書，時人謂之「斜封官」；

translations.literal: Princesses Anle and Changning, the empress's younger sister the Lady of Chengguo, the Brilliant Consort Shangguan, the Brilliant Consort's mother the Lady of Pei, Zheng, the Palace Mistress Chai, Lady Helou, the witch Diwu Ying'er, and the Lady of Longxi, Zhao—all relied on their power to handle affairs, accepted bribes for petitions and audiences; even butchers, peddlers, and menials, with three hundred thousand cash, could receive a separate imperial rescript appointing them to office, sent slant-sealed to the Secretariat—people of the time called them 'slant-seal appointments';
translations.idiomatic: Princesses Anle and Changning, the empress's younger sister the Lady of Chengguo, the Brilliant Consort Shangguan, the Brilliant Consort's mother the Lady of Pei, Zheng, the Palace Mistress Chai, Lady Helou, the witch Diwu Ying'er, and the Lady of Longxi, Zhao—all relied on their power to handle affairs and accepted bribes for petitions and audiences; even butchers, peddlers, and menials, with three hundred thousand cash, could receive a separate imperial rescript appointing them to office, sent slant-sealed to the Secretariat—people of the time called them 'slant-seal appointments';

sentences.zh: 錢三萬則度爲僧尼。

translations.literal: with thirty thousand cash one could be tonsured as monk or nun.
translations.idiomatic: with thirty thousand cash one could be tonsured as monk or nun.

sentences.zh: 其員外、同正、試、攝、檢校、判、知官凡數千人。

translations.literal: Their supernumerary, co-regular, probationary, acting, inspector, vice-, and acting-charge appointments numbered several thousand in all.
translations.idiomatic: Their supernumerary, co-regular, probationary, acting, inspector, vice-, and acting-charge appointments numbered several thousand in all.

sentences.zh: 西京、東都各置兩吏部侍郎，爲四銓，選者歳數萬人。

translations.literal: Western Capital and Eastern Capital each had two Vice Directors of the Ministry of Personnel, making four selection boards, with tens of thousands chosen each year.
translations.idiomatic: Western Capital and Eastern Capital each had two Vice Directors of the Ministry of Personnel, making four selection boards, with tens of thousands chosen each year.

sentences.zh: 上官婕妤及後宮多立外第，出入無節，朝士往往從之遊處，以求進達。

translations.literal: The Brilliant Consort Shangguan and many in the rear palace established outer mansions; their comings and goings knew no restraint, and court gentlemen often joined them in pleasure to seek advancement.
translations.idiomatic: The Brilliant Consort Shangguan and many in the rear palace established outer mansions; their comings and goings knew no restraint, and court gentlemen often joined them in pleasure to seek advancement.

sentences.zh: 安樂公主尤驕橫，宰相以下多出其門。

translations.literal: Princess Anle was especially arrogant and overbearing; most men from chancellor down issued from her gate.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Anle was especially arrogant and overbearing; most men from chancellor down issued from her gate.

sentences.zh: 與長樂公主競起第捨，以侈麗相髙，擬於宮掖，而精巧過之。

translations.literal: She vied with Princess Changle in raising mansions, each striving to outdo the other in lavish splendor, rivaling the palace precincts—and surpassing them in refinement.
translations.idiomatic: She vied with Princess Changle in raising mansions, each striving to outdo the other in lavish splendor, rivaling the palace precincts—and surpassing them in refinement.

sentences.zh: 安樂公主請昆明池，上以百姓蒲魚所資，不許。

translations.literal: Princess Anle requested Kunming Pond; the emperor said the common people relied on it for rushes and fish and would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Anle requested Kunming Pond; the emperor said the common people relied on it for rushes and fish and would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 公主不悅，乃更奪民田作定昆池，延袤數里，累石像華山，引水象天津，欲以勝昆明，故名定昆。

translations.literal: The princess was displeased and instead seized commoners' fields to make the Dingkun Pond, extending several li; stones were piled to resemble Mount Hua, and water was drawn to imitate the Heavenly Ford, intending to surpass Kunming—hence the name Dingkun ('Fixed Kun').
translations.idiomatic: The princess was displeased and instead seized commoners' fields to make the Dingkun Pond, extending several li; stones were piled to resemble Mount Hua, and water was drawn to imitate the Heavenly Ford, intending to surpass Kunming—hence the name Dingkun ('Fixed Kun').

sentences.zh: 安樂有織成裙，直錢一億，花卉鳥獸，皆如粟粒，正視旁視，日中影中，各爲一色。

translations.literal: Anle had a woven skirt worth a hundred million cash; flowers, birds, and beasts were all like millet grains—from straight view, side view, noon, or shadow, each showed a different color.
translations.idiomatic: Anle had a woven skirt worth a hundred million cash; flowers, birds, and beasts were all like millet grains—from straight view, side view, noon, or shadow, each showed a different color.

sentences.zh: 上好撃毯，由是風俗相尚，駙馬武崇訓、楊愼交灑油以築毯塲。

translations.literal: The emperor loved to play cuju, and thereby the custom came to be admired; the imperial sons-in-law Wu Chongxun and Yang Shenjiao poured oil to build cuju grounds.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor loved to play cuju, and thereby the custom came to be admired; the imperial sons-in-law Wu Chongxun and Yang Shenjiao poured oil to build cuju grounds.

sentences.zh: 愼交，恭仁曾孫也。

translations.literal: Shenjiao was a great-great-grandson of Gongren.
translations.idiomatic: Shenjiao was a great-great-grandson of Yang Gongren.

sentences.zh: 上及皇后、公主多營佛寺。

translations.literal: The emperor, empress, and princesses largely built Buddhist temples.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, empress, and princesses largely built Buddhist temples.

sentences.zh: 左拾遺京兆辛替否上疎諫，略曰：「臣聞古之建官，員不必備，士有完行，家有廉節，朝廷有餘俸，百姓有餘食。

translations.literal: Left Reminder Xintifou of Jingzhao submitted a remonstrance, in part: "I have heard that in antiquity when offices were established, posts need not all be filled; scholars had complete conduct, families had integrity, the court had surplus salaries, and the people had surplus food.
translations.idiomatic: Left Reminder Xintifou of Jingzhao submitted a remonstrance, in part: "I have heard that in antiquity when offices were established, posts need not all be filled; scholars had complete conduct, families had integrity, the court had surplus salaries, and the people had surplus food.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下百倍行賞，十倍增官，金銀不供其印，束帛不充於錫，遂使富商豪賈，居盡纓冕之流；

translations.literal: I consider that Your Majesty bestows rewards a hundredfold and multiplies offices tenfold; gold and silver cannot supply their seals, silks cannot fill their gifts—so that great merchants and powerful traders now fill the ranks of capped and girdled officials;
translations.idiomatic: I consider that Your Majesty bestows rewards a hundredfold and multiplies offices tenfold; gold and silver cannot supply their seals, silks cannot fill their gifts—so that great merchants and powerful traders now fill the ranks of capped and girdled officials;

sentences.zh: 鬻伎行巫，或渉膏腴之地。」

translations.literal: those who sold their arts or practiced witchcraft sometimes trod on rich and fertile lands."
translations.idiomatic: those who sold their arts or practiced witchcraft sometimes trod on rich and fertile lands."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「公主，陛下之愛女，然而用不合於古義，行不根於人心，將恐變愛成憎，翻福爲禍。

translations.literal: He also said: "The princess is Your Majesty's beloved daughter, yet her use does not accord with ancient principle and her conduct is not rooted in the people's hearts—I fear love may turn to hatred and blessing to calamity.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "The princess is Your Majesty's beloved daughter, yet her use does not accord with ancient principle and her conduct is not rooted in the people's hearts—I fear love may turn to hatred and blessing to calamity.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 竭人之力，費人之財，奪人之家；

translations.literal: To exhaust people's strength, spend people's wealth, and seize people's homes;
translations.idiomatic: To exhaust people's strength, spend people's wealth, and seize people's homes;

sentences.zh: 愛數子而取三怨，使邊疆之士不盡力，朝廷之士不盡忠，人之散矣，獨持所愛，何所恃乎！

translations.literal: to love a few children yet incur three hatreds, to make frontier soldiers not exert their strength and court gentlemen not give their loyalty—when the people are scattered, what can you rely on if you hold only those you love!
translations.idiomatic: to love a few children yet incur three hatreds, to make frontier soldiers not exert their strength and court gentlemen not give their loyalty—when the people are scattered, what can you rely on if you hold only those you love!

sentences.zh: 君以人爲本，本固則邦寧，邦寧則陛下之夫婦母子長相保也。」

translations.literal: The ruler takes the people as his root; when the root is firm the state is tranquil, and when the state is tranquil Your Majesty's husband and wife, mother and sons may long preserve one another."
translations.idiomatic: The ruler takes the people as his root; when the root is firm the state is tranquil, and when the state is tranquil Your Majesty's husband and wife, mother and sons may long preserve one another."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「若以造寺必爲理體，養人不足經邦，則殷、周已往皆暗亂，漢、魏已降皆聖明，殷、周已往爲不長，漢、魏已降爲不短矣。

translations.literal: He also said: "If building temples must be the principle of governance and nourishing the people is insufficient to rule the state, then Yin and Zhou and before were all benighted and chaotic, while Han, Wei, and after were all sage and bright—Yin and Zhou and before did not last long, Han and Wei and after did not fall short.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "If building temples must be the principle of governance and nourishing the people is insufficient to rule the state, then Yin and Zhou and before were all benighted and chaotic, while Han, Wei, and after were all sage and bright—Yin and Zhou and before did not last long, Han and Wei and after did not fall short.

sentences.zh: 陛下緩其所急，急其所緩，親未來而疎見在，失眞實而冀虚無，重俗人之爲，輕天子之業，雖以陰陽爲炭，萬物以銅，役不食之人，使不衣之士，猶尚不給，況資於天生地養，風動雨潤，而後得之乎！

translations.literal: Your Majesty is slow where you should be urgent and urgent where you should be slow; you are close to what has not yet come and distant from what is present; you lose what is real and hope for what is empty; you weight the deeds of vulgar men and slight the enterprise of the Son of Heaven—even if yin and yang were fuel and the myriad things copper, and you employed men who do not eat and made men who do not dress work, it would still not suffice—how much less when you rely on what Heaven generates and Earth nourishes, what wind stirs and rain moistens, and only then obtain it!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is slow where you should be urgent and urgent where you should be slow; you are close to what has not yet come and distant from what is present; you lose what is real and hope for what is empty; you weight the deeds of vulgar men and slight the enterprise of the Son of Heaven—even if yin and yang were fuel and the myriad things copper, and you employed men who do not eat and made men who do not dress work, it would still not suffice—how much less when you rely on what Heaven generates and Earth nourishes, what wind stirs and rain moistens, and only then obtain it!

sentences.zh: 一旦風塵再擾，霜雹荐臻，沙彌不可操干戈，寺塔不足攘饑饉，臣竊惜之。」

translations.literal: Once dust and turmoil rise again and frost and hail come in succession, shramanas cannot wield weapons and temple towers cannot repel famine—I privately lament this."
translations.idiomatic: Once dust and turmoil rise again and frost and hail come in succession, shramanas cannot wield weapons and temple towers cannot repel famine—I privately lament this."

sentences.zh: 疎奏，不省。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted, but the emperor took no notice.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted, but the emperor took no notice.

sentences.zh: 時斜封官皆不由兩省而授，兩省莫敢執奏，即宣示所司。

translations.literal: At this time slant-seal appointments were all conferred without passing through the two departments; the two departments did not dare to memorialize objections and simply announced them to the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: At this time slant-seal appointments were all conferred without passing through the two departments; the two departments did not dare to memorialize objections and simply announced them to the responsible offices.

sentences.zh: 吏部員外郎李朝隱前後執破一千四百餘人，怨謗紛然，朝隱一無所顧。

translations.literal: Li Chaoyin, Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel, on repeated occasions blocked more than fourteen hundred such appointments; complaints and slanders swarmed, yet Chaoyin paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chaoyin, Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel, on repeated occasions blocked more than fourteen hundred such appointments; complaints and slanders swarmed, yet Chaoyin paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，己酉，修文館直學士、直居舍人武平一上表請抑損外戚權寵；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on jiyou, Wu Pingyi, Direct Academician of the Xiuxuan Hall and Direct Palace Scribe, submitted a memorial requesting curtailment of the power and favor of maternal kin;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on jiyou, Wu Pingyi, Direct Academician of the Xiuxuan Hall and Direct Palace Scribe, submitted a memorial requesting curtailment of the power and favor of maternal kin;

sentences.zh: 不敢斥言韋氏，但請抑損己家。

translations.literal: he did not dare name the Wei clan openly but only asked to curtail his own family.
translations.idiomatic: he did not dare name the Wei clan openly but only asked to curtail his own family.

sentences.zh: 上優制不許。

translations.literal: The emperor issued a gracious edict and did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued a gracious edict and did not permit it.

sentences.zh: 平一名甄，以字行，載德之子也。

translations.literal: Pingyi's given name was Zhen; he went by his style name and was a son of Zaidé.
translations.idiomatic: Pingyi's given name was Zhen; he went by his style name and was a son of Wu Zaidé.

sentences.zh: 十一月，庚申，突騎施酋長娑葛自立爲可汗，殺唐使者御史中丞馮嘉賓，遣其弟遮努等帥衆犯塞。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on gengshen, Suoge, chieftain of the Qarlugs, declared himself qaghan, killed the Tang envoy, Vice Censor-in-Chief Feng Jiabin, and sent his younger brother Zhenu and others to lead troops in raiding the border.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on gengshen, Suoge, chieftain of the Qarlugs, declared himself qaghan, killed the Tang envoy, Vice Censor-in-Chief Feng Jiabin, and sent his younger brother Zhenu and others to lead troops in raiding the border.

sentences.zh: 初，娑葛既代烏質勒統衆，父時故將闕啜忠節不服，數相攻撃。

translations.literal: Initially, after Suoge had succeeded Wuzhile in commanding the tribes, the former general Quechuo Zhongjie would not submit and they repeatedly attacked one another.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, after Suoge had succeeded Wuzhile in commanding the tribes, the former general Quechuo Zhongjie would not submit and they repeatedly attacked one another.

sentences.zh: 忠節衆弱不能支，金山道行軍總管郭元振奏追忠節入朝宿衞。

translations.literal: Zhongjie's forces were weak and could not hold out; Guo Yuanzhen, Commander on Campaign of the Jinshan Circuit, memorialized to summon Zhongjie to court for palace guard duty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongjie's forces were weak and could not hold out; Guo Yuanzhen, Commander on Campaign of the Jinshan Circuit, memorialized to summon Zhongjie to court for palace guard duty.

sentences.zh: 忠節行至播仙城，經略使、右威衞將軍周以悌説之曰：「國家不愛髙官顯爵以待君者，以君有部落之衆故也。

translations.literal: When Zhongjie reached Boxian City, the Commissioner for Pacification and General of the Right Weiwu Guard, Zhou Yiti, persuaded him: "The state does not withhold high office and splendid rank awaiting you because you command a tribal following.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongjie reached Boxian City, the Commissioner for Pacification and General of the Right Weiwu Guard, Zhou Yiti, persuaded him: "The state does not withhold high office and splendid rank awaiting you because you command a tribal following.

sentences.zh: 今脱身入朝，一老胡耳。

translations.literal: Now if you leave your body and enter court, you are but one old barbarian.
translations.idiomatic: Now if you leave your following and enter court, you are but one old barbarian.

sentences.zh: 豈惟不保寵祿，死生亦制於人手。

translations.literal: Not only will you not preserve favor and salary—life and death will also be in another's hands.
translations.idiomatic: Not only will you not preserve favor and salary—life and death will also be in another's hands.

sentences.zh: 方今宰相宗楚客、紀處訥用事，不若厚賂二公，請留不行，發安西兵及引吐蕃以撃娑葛，求阿史那獻爲可汗以招十姓，使郭虔瓘發拔汗那兵以自助；

translations.literal: At present the chancellors Zong Chuke and Ji Chuna hold power—better to bribe the two lords richly, ask to stay and not go, dispatch Anxi troops and bring in Tibet to strike Suoge, seek Ashina Xian as qaghan to win over the Ten Surnames, and have Guo Qianzhen raise Ferghana troops to assist yourself;
translations.idiomatic: At present the chancellors Zong Chuke and Ji Chuna hold power—better to bribe the two lords richly, ask to stay and not go, dispatch Anxi troops and bring in Tibet to strike Suoge, seek Ashina Xian as qaghan to win over the Ten Surnames, and have Guo Qianzhen raise Ferghana troops to assist yourself;

sentences.zh: 既不失部落，又得報仇，比於入朝，豈可同日語哉！」

translations.literal: you will neither lose your tribes nor fail to gain revenge—how can this be spoken of in the same day as entering court!"
translations.idiomatic: you will neither lose your tribes nor fail to gain revenge—how can this be spoken of in the same day as entering court!"

sentences.zh: 郭虔瓘者，歴城人，時爲西邊將。

translations.literal: Guo Qianzhen was a man of Licheng and at this time was a western frontier general.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Qianzhen was a man of Licheng and at this time was a western frontier general.

sentences.zh: 忠節然其言，遣間使賂楚客、處訥，請如以悌之策。

translations.literal: Zhongjie approved his words and sent secret envoys to bribe Chuke and Chuna, requesting according to Yiti's plan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongjie approved his words and sent secret envoys to bribe Chuke and Chuna, requesting according to Yiti's plan.

sentences.zh: 元振聞其謀，上疎，以爲：「往歳吐蕃所以犯邊，正爲求十姓、四鎭之地不獲故耳。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen heard of the plot and submitted a memorial, stating: "In former years Tibet raided the border precisely because it could not obtain the lands of the Ten Surnames and the Four Garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen heard of the plot and submitted a memorial, stating: "In former years Tibet raided the border precisely because it could not obtain the lands of the Ten Surnames and the Four Garrisons.

sentences.zh: 比者息兵請和，非能慕悅中國之禮義也，直以國多内難，人畜疫癘，恐中國乘其弊，故且屈志求自暱。

translations.literal: Recently it ceased arms and sought peace—not because it could admire China's rites and righteousness, but simply because the state had many internal troubles and men and livestock suffered pestilence; fearing China would seize its weakness, it therefore bent its will for the moment to seek closeness.
translations.idiomatic: Recently it ceased arms and sought peace—not because it could admire China's rites and righteousness, but simply because the state had many internal troubles and men and livestock suffered pestilence; fearing China would seize its weakness, it therefore bent its will for the moment to seek closeness.

sentences.zh: 使其國小安，豈能忘取十姓、四鎭之地哉！

translations.literal: If its state grows slightly secure, how could it forget to take the lands of the Ten Surnames and Four Garrisons!
translations.idiomatic: If its state grows slightly secure, how could it forget to take the lands of the Ten Surnames and Four Garrisons!

sentences.zh: 今忠節不論國家大計，直欲爲吐蕃鄕導，恐四鎭危機，將從此始。

translations.literal: Now Zhongjie, heedless of the state's great plan, wishes directly to serve Tibet as a native guide—I fear the crisis of the Four Garrisons will begin from this.
translations.idiomatic: Now Zhongjie, heedless of the state's great plan, wishes directly to serve Tibet as a native guide—I fear the crisis of the Four Garrisons will begin from this.

sentences.zh: 頃縁默啜憑陵，所應者多，兼四鎭兵疲弊，勢未能爲忠節經略，非憐突騎施也。

translations.literal: Recently, because Mokchuo pressed hard, there were many demands to answer, and the troops of the Four Garrisons were worn and exhausted—the situation could not undertake strategy for Zhongjie; it was not pity for the Qarlugs.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, because Mokchuo pressed hard, there were many demands to answer, and the troops of the Four Garrisons were worn and exhausted—the situation could not undertake strategy for Zhongjie; it was not pity for the Qarlugs.

sentences.zh: 忠節不體國家中外之意而更求吐蕃；

translations.literal: Zhongjie does not grasp the court's intent at home and abroad yet seeks Tibet instead;
translations.idiomatic: Zhongjie does not grasp the court's intent at home and abroad yet seeks Tibet instead;

sentences.zh: 吐蕃得志，則忠節在其掌握，豈得復事唐也！

translations.literal: if Tibet gains its wish, then Zhongjie will be in its grasp—how could he again serve Tang!
translations.idiomatic: if Tibet gains its wish, then Zhongjie will be in its grasp—how could he again serve Tang!

sentences.zh: 往年吐蕃無恩於中國，猶欲求十姓、四鎭之地；

translations.literal: In former years Tibet owed China no kindness, yet still sought the lands of the Ten Surnames and Four Garrisons;
translations.idiomatic: In former years Tibet owed China no kindness, yet still sought the lands of the Ten Surnames and Four Garrisons;

sentences.zh: 今若破娑葛有功，請分于闐、疎勒，不知以何理抑之！

translations.literal: now if it breaks Suoge with merit and requests a share of Khotan and Shule, by what principle could we refuse!
translations.idiomatic: now if it breaks Suoge with merit and requests a share of Khotan and Shule, by what principle could we refuse!

sentences.zh: 又，其所部諸蠻及婆羅門等方不服，若借唐兵助討之，亦不知以何詞拒之！

translations.literal: Moreover, the various barbarians under its command and the Brahmins and others are not yet submissive; if it borrows Tang troops to help chastise them, by what words could we refuse!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the various barbarians under its command and the Brahmins and others are not yet submissive; if it borrows Tang troops to help chastise them, by what words could we refuse!

sentences.zh: 是以古之智者皆不願受夷狄之惠，蓋豫憂其求請無厭、終爲後患故也。

translations.literal: Therefore the wise of antiquity were all unwilling to accept favors from the barbarians, because they foresaw that their requests would know no satiety and would in the end become later troubles.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the wise of antiquity were all unwilling to accept favors from the barbarians, because they foresaw that their requests would know no satiety and would in the end become later troubles.

sentences.zh: 又，彼請阿史那獻者，豈非以獻爲可汗子孫，欲依之以招懷十姓乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, in their request for Ashina Xian—is it not because Xian is a descendant of the qaghan and they wish to rely on him to win over and comfort the Ten Surnames?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in their request for Ashina Xian—is it not because Xian is a descendant of the qaghan and they wish to rely on him to win over and comfort the Ten Surnames?

sentences.zh: 按獻父元慶，叔父僕羅，兄俀子及斛瑟羅、懷道等，皆可汗子孫也。

translations.literal: Examining the case: Xian's father Yuanking, his uncle Boklu, his elder brothers Kouzi, Huseluo, Huaidao, and the like—all are descendants of the qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: Consider the record: Xian's father Yuanking, his uncle Boklu, his elder brothers Kouzi, Huseluo, Huaidao, and others—all were descendants of the qaghan.

sentences.zh: 往者唐及吐蕃遍曾立之以爲可汗，欲以招撫十姓，皆不能致，尋自破滅。

translations.literal: In former times Tang and Tibet repeatedly established them as qaghan, wishing by this to win and pacify the Ten Surnames—all failed to bring them in, and soon they perished of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In the past, both Tang and Tibet had repeatedly installed them as qaghan, hoping to win over and pacify the Ten Surnames—yet none succeeded, and each soon collapsed on his own.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why is this so?
translations.idiomatic: Why was this?

sentences.zh: 此屬非有過人之才，恩威不足以動衆，雖復可汗舊種，衆心終不親附，況獻又疎遠於其父兄乎？

translations.literal: This sort lacked outstanding talent; grace and severity were insufficient to move the multitude. Though they were again the old qaghan stock, the hearts of the masses ultimately would not draw close and attach—and how much more so Xian, who is even more remote than his father and elder brothers?
translations.idiomatic: Men of this stripe possessed no exceptional talent; their grace and severity were not enough to sway the tribes. Though they bore the old qaghan blood, the people never truly rallied to them—and Xian stands even farther from his father and brothers in lineage and standing.

sentences.zh: 若使忠節兵力自能誘脅十姓，則不必求立可汗子孫也。

translations.literal: If Zhongjie's military strength could by itself entice and coerce the Ten Surnames, then there would be no need to seek to install a qaghan's descendant.
translations.idiomatic: If Zhongjie's forces alone could lure and compel the Ten Surnames, there would be no need to install some qaghan's descendant at all.

sentences.zh: 又，欲令郭虔瓘入拔汗都，發其兵。

translations.literal: Moreover, they wish to have Guo Qianzhen enter Bokhara and raise its troops.
translations.idiomatic: They also propose sending Guo Qianzhen into Ferghana to mobilize its forces.

sentences.zh: 虔瓘前此已嘗與忠書擅入拔汗那發兵，不能得其片甲匹馬，而拔汗那不勝侵擾，常引此番，奉俀子，還侵四鎭。

translations.literal: Qianzhen, earlier in this matter, had already on Zhongjie's letter entered Ferghana without authorization to raise troops and could not obtain so much as a single suit of armor or horse—but Ferghana, unable to bear the harassment, repeatedly brought in this Turgesh faction, enthroned Kouzi, and returned to raid the Four Garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhen had already once, on Zhongjie's orders, entered Ferghana without authorization to raise troops and gained not a single suit of armor or horse—while Ferghana, unable to endure the raids, kept bringing in the Turgesh, enthroning Kouzi and turning back to harry the Four Garrisons.

sentences.zh: 時拔汗那四旁無強寇爲援，虔瓘等恣爲侵掠，如獨行無人之境，猶引俀子爲患。

translations.literal: At that time Ferghana had no strong enemy on its four sides to lend aid; Qianzhen and the rest indulged in plunder as if walking alone through an uninhabited realm—yet still Kouzi was brought in as a trouble.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, Ferghana had no powerful enemy nearby to turn to for help, and Qianzhen's men plundered at will as though crossing empty country—yet even then Kouzi was brought in and became a scourge.

sentences.zh: 今北有娑葛，急則與之並力，内則諸胡堅壁拒守，外則突厥伺隙邀遮。

translations.literal: Now to the north there is Suoge—if pressed, he will join forces with them; within, the various foreign peoples will hold fast behind walls and refuse to yield; without, the Turks will watch for openings and intercept.
translations.idiomatic: Now Suoge lies to the north and would join forces with them in an emergency; within, the frontier peoples would bar their gates and refuse to fight; without, the Turks would watch for weakness and cut off their retreat.

sentences.zh: 臣料虔瓘等此行，必不能如往年之得志；

translations.literal: Your servant calculates that on this expedition Qianzhen and the rest will surely be unable to succeed as in former years;
translations.idiomatic: I judge that on this expedition Qianzhen and his men cannot achieve what they did in years past;

sentences.zh: 内外受敵，自陷危亡，徒與虜結隙，令四鎭不安。

translations.literal: Attacked within and without, they will themselves fall into peril and ruin, vainly creating enmity with the barbarians and leaving the Four Garrisons unquiet.
translations.idiomatic: Beset from within and without, they will only court disaster, needlessly alienate the frontier tribes, and leave the Four Garrisons in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 以臣愚揣之，實爲非計。」

translations.literal: By your servant's foolish reckoning, this is truly a bad plan."
translations.idiomatic: In my humble judgment, this is a misguided policy altogether.

sentences.zh: 楚客等不從，建議：「遣馮嘉賓持節安撫忠節，侍御史呂守素處置四鎭，以將軍牛師獎爲安西副都護，發甘、涼以西兵，兼征吐蕃，以討娑葛。」

translations.literal: Chuke and the rest did not follow this advice and proposed: "Send Feng Jiabin bearing credentials to pacify Zhongjie, the attendant censor Lü Shousu to manage the Four Garrisons, and the general Niu Shijiang as Vice Protector-General of Anxi; mobilize troops west of Gan and Liang, and also summon Tibet, to chastise Suoge."
translations.idiomatic: Chuke and his faction rejected the memorial and proposed instead: "Dispatch Feng Jiabin with imperial credentials to pacify Zhongjie, attendant censor Lü Shousu to administer the Four Garrisons, and General Niu Shijiang as Vice Protector-General of Anxi; raise the armies west of Gan and Liang, and enlist Tibet as well, to campaign against Suoge."

sentences.zh: 娑葛遣使娑臘獻馬在京師，聞其謀，馳還報娑葛。

translations.literal: Suoge sent the envoy Sola to present horses at the capital; hearing of the plot, he galloped back to report to Suoge.
translations.idiomatic: Suoge had sent his envoy Sola to the capital to present horses; when Sola learned of the plan, he raced back to warn Suoge.

sentences.zh: 於是娑葛發五千騎出安西，五千騎出撥換，五千騎出焉耆，五千騎出疎勒，入寇。

translations.literal: Thereupon Suoge dispatched five thousand horsemen out of Anxi, five thousand out of Boli, five thousand out of Yanqi, and five thousand out of Shule—to raid in.
translations.idiomatic: Suoge then sent five thousand horsemen from Anxi, five thousand from Boli, five thousand from Yanqi, and five thousand from Shule—all raiding the frontier.

sentences.zh: 元振在疎勒，柵於河口，不敢出。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen was at Shule, palisaded at the river mouth, and dared not go out.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen was at Shule, entrenched at the river mouth, and dared not emerge.

sentences.zh: 忠節逆嘉賓於計舒河口，娑葛遣兵襲入，生擒忠節，殺嘉賓，擒呂守素於僻城，縛於驛柱，冎而殺之。

translations.literal: Zhongjie intercepted Jiabin at the mouth of the Jishu River; Suoge sent troops in a surprise attack, took Zhongjie alive, killed Jiabin, seized Lü Shousu in a remote town, bound him to a relay-post pillar, beheaded him, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongjie intercepted Jiabin at the mouth of the Jishu River; Suoge sent troops in a surprise attack, took Zhongjie alive, killed Jiabin, captured Lü Shousu in a remote town, bound him to a relay-post pillar, beheaded him, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 上以安樂公主將適左衞中郎將武延秀，遣使召太子賓客武攸緒於嵩山。

translations.literal: Because the emperor's daughter Princess Anle was about to marry the Left Guard Palace Attendant Wu Yanxiu, he sent envoys to summon the Crown Prince's Guest Wu Youxu from Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: As Princess Anle was to marry Left Guard Palace Attendant Wu Yanxiu, the emperor sent envoys to summon Crown Prince's Guest Wu Youxu from Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 攸緒將至，上敕禮官於兩儀殿設別位，欲行問道之禮，聽以山服葛巾入見，不名不拜。

translations.literal: When Youxu was about to arrive, the emperor ordered the ritual officers to set a separate seat in the Hall of Two Appearances, intending to perform the rite of inquiring after the Way, allowing him to enter audience in mountain garb and hemp cap, without being named and without bowing.
translations.idiomatic: As Youxu was nearing the capital, the emperor ordered ritual officers to prepare a separate seat in the Hall of Two Appearances for a rite of inquiring after the Way, permitting him to attend in rustic mountain dress and hemp cap, without being addressed by name or required to bow.

sentences.zh: 仗入，通事舍人引攸緒就位；

translations.literal: When the imperial guard entered, the protocol master led Youxu to his place;
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial guard entered, the protocol officer escorted Youxu to his place;

sentences.zh: 攸緒趨立辭見班中，再拜如常儀。

translations.literal: Youxu hastened to stand in the farewell-audience formation and bowed twice according to ordinary rite.
translations.idiomatic: Youxu hurried to take his place in the regular greeting formation and bowed twice according to ordinary court etiquette.

sentences.zh: 上愕然，竟不成所擬之禮。

translations.literal: The emperor was startled; in the end the ceremony as planned was not completed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was taken aback; the planned ceremony never took place.

sentences.zh: 上屢延之内殿，頻煩寵錫，皆謝不受；

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly invited him to the inner hall and lavished favor upon him, but he declined all and accepted nothing;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repeatedly summoned him to the inner palace and showered him with honors, but he declined them all;

sentences.zh: 親貴謁侯，寒温之外，不交一言。

translations.literal: When nobles and the eminent called on him, beyond inquiries after cold and warmth he exchanged not a single word.
translations.idiomatic: When kinsmen and high officials came to call, he spoke not a word beyond the customary greetings.

sentences.zh: 初，武崇訓之尚公主也，延秀數得侍宴。

translations.literal: At first, when Wu Chongxun married the princess, Yanxiu repeatedly gained attendance at banquets.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Wu Chongxun married the princess, Yanxiu had often been present at imperial banquets.

sentences.zh: 延秀美姿儀，善歌舞，公主悅之。

translations.literal: Yanxiu had handsome bearing and was skilled in song and dance; the princess was pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxiu was handsome and skilled in song and dance, and the princess took a liking to him.

sentences.zh: 及崇訓死，遂以延秀尚焉。

translations.literal: When Chongxun died, she then took Yanxiu in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: After Chongxun died, she married Yanxiu in his place.

sentences.zh: 己卯，成禮，假皇后仗，分禁兵以盛其儀衞，命安國相王障車。

translations.literal: On jimao the marriage rites were completed; the empress's guard of honor was borrowed, palace troops were distributed to magnify the ceremonial escort, and the Prince of An'guo was ordered to escort the bridal carriage.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao the wedding was completed; the empress's guard of honor was borrowed, palace troops were deployed to enlarge the ceremonial escort, and the Prince of An'guo was appointed to escort the bridal carriage.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，赦天下。

translations.literal: On gengchen, an amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen the emperor proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 以延秀爲太常卿，兼右衞將軍。

translations.literal: Yanxiu was made Grand Master of Ceremonies and concurrently General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxiu was appointed Grand Master of Ceremonies and concurrently General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，宴群臣於兩儀殿，命公主出拜公卿，公卿皆伏地稽首。

translations.literal: On xinsi the emperor feasted the hundred officials in the Hall of Two Appearances, ordered the princess to come out and bow to the public ministers, and the public ministers all prostrated themselves and kowtowed.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi the emperor held a banquet for the court in the Hall of Two Appearances, had the princess come forward to bow to the ministers, and every minister prostrated himself in reply.

sentences.zh: 癸未，牛師獎與突騎施娑葛戰於火燒城，師獎兵敗沒。

translations.literal: On guiwei, Niu Shijiang fought Suoge of the Qarlugs at Fire-Burned City; Shijiang's army was defeated and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, Niu Shijiang battled Suoge of the Qarlugs at Fire-Burned City; Shijiang's army was annihilated in defeat.

sentences.zh: 娑葛遂陷安西，斷四鎭路，遣使上表，求宗楚客頭。

translations.literal: Suoge then captured Anxi, cut the roads of the Four Garrisons, and sent envoys with a memorial requesting Zong Chuke's head.
translations.idiomatic: Suoge then seized Anxi, severed the routes to the Four Garrisons, and sent a memorial demanding Zong Chuke's head.

sentences.zh: 楚客又奏以周以悌代郭元振統衆，征元振入朝；

translations.literal: Chuke again memorialized that Zhou Yiti replace Guo Yuanzhen in commanding the forces and that Yuanzhen be summoned to court;
translations.idiomatic: Chuke again memorialized to replace Guo Yuanzhen with Zhou Yiti in command of the frontier armies and to recall Yuanzhen to court;

sentences.zh: 以阿史那獻爲十姓可汗，置軍焉耆以討娑葛。

translations.literal: Ashina Xian was made qaghan of the Ten Surnames, and an army was stationed at Yanqi to chastise Suoge.
translations.idiomatic: Ashina Xian was installed as qaghan of the Ten Surnames, and troops were posted at Yanqi to campaign against Suoge.

sentences.zh: 娑葛遺元振書，稱：「我與唐初無惡，但仇闕啜。

translations.literal: Suoge sent Yuanzhen a letter, stating: "From the first I had no ill will toward Tang—I bear hatred only for Queluo.
translations.idiomatic: Suoge wrote to Yuanzhen: "From the first I bore Tang no ill will; my enmity is for Queluo alone.

sentences.zh: 宗尚書受闕啜金，欲枉破奴部落，馮中丞、牛都護相繼而來，奴豈得坐而待死！

translations.literal: Minister Zong received gold from Queluo and wished to wrongly destroy my tribes—Commissioner Feng and Protector Niu came one after another; how could your slave sit and await death!
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zong took Queluo's gold and sought to destroy my tribes unjustly—Commissioner Feng and Protector Niu came one after another; am I to sit and wait for death?

sentences.zh: 又聞史獻欲來，徒擾軍師，恐未有寧日。

translations.literal: I also hear that Shi Xian is about to come—that will only trouble the army and frontier; I fear there will be no day of peace.
translations.idiomatic: I also hear that Ashina Xian is to be sent—this will only throw the army and frontier into chaos, and I fear there will be no peace.

sentences.zh: 乞大使商量處置。」

translations.literal: I beg the ambassador to consult and settle the matter."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the envoy discuss the matter and arrange a settlement."

sentences.zh: 元振奏娑葛書。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen memorialized Suoge's letter.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen submitted Suoge's letter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 楚客怒，奏言元振有異圖，召，將罪之。

translations.literal: Chuke was angry and memorialized that Yuanzhen harbored a different design; he was summoned and about to be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Chuke flew into a rage and memorialized that Yuanzhen harbored subversive intentions; Yuanzhen was summoned and about to be punished.

sentences.zh: 元振使其子鴻間道具奏其狀，乞留定西土，不敢歸。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen had his son Hong send a secret memorial stating his situation, begging to remain and secure the western lands and not daring to return.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen had his son Hong send a secret memorial outlining the situation, begging to remain on the western frontier and pleading not to be recalled.

sentences.zh: 周以悌竟坐流白州，復以元振代以悌，赦娑葛罪，冊爲十四姓可汗。

translations.literal: Zhou Yiti in the end was punished by exile to Baizhou; Yuanzhen was again put in Yiti's place; Suoge's crimes were pardoned and he was enfeoffed as qaghan of the Fourteen Surnames.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yiti was ultimately exiled to Baizhou; Yuanzhen was reappointed in his place; Suoge was pardoned and invested as qaghan of the Fourteen Surnames.

sentences.zh: 以婕妤上官氏爲昭容。

translations.literal: The Lady of Handsome Fairness, Lady Shangguan, was made Brilliant Lady.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Shangguan, a Lady of Handsome Fairness, was appointed Brilliant Lady.

sentences.zh: 十二月，御史中丞姚廷筠奏稱：「比見諸司不遵律令格式，事無大小皆悉聞奏。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the Censor-in-Chief Yao Tingyun memorialized: "Recently I have seen the various offices not follow statutes, ordinances, and protocols; matters great and small are all reported for imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Censor-in-Chief Yao Tingyun memorialized: "Of late I have seen offices ignore statutes and regulations and refer every matter, great or small, to the throne for decision.

sentences.zh: 臣聞爲君者任臣，爲臣者奉法。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that the ruler for his part employs his ministers, and the minister for his part upholds the law.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard it said that a ruler entrusts affairs to his ministers, and ministers uphold the law.

sentences.zh: 萬機叢委，不可遍覽，豈有修一水竇，伐一枯木，皆取斷宸衷！

translations.literal: A myriad of affairs crowd in submission—they cannot all be surveyed; how could repairing a water channel or felling a withered tree all require judgment from the imperial heart!
translations.idiomatic: Affairs of state are innumerable and cannot all be reviewed—surely not every repair of a water channel or felling of a dead tree should await the emperor's personal judgment!

sentences.zh: 自今若軍國大事及條式無文者，聽奏取進止，自餘各准法處分。

translations.literal: From today onward, if there are great military and state affairs and cases where the regulations have no written provision, let memorials be submitted for imperial decision; all the rest shall each be handled according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth only major military and state affairs, and cases for which no regulation exists, should be brought to the throne; all others should be handled according to law.

sentences.zh: 其有故生疑滯，致有稽失，望令御史糾彈。」

translations.literal: If any deliberately foster doubt and delay, causing neglect and loss, I hope the censors may be ordered to investigate and impeach."
translations.idiomatic: When officials deliberately raise doubts or cause delay and neglect, I ask that the censors be empowered to investigate and impeach them."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 丁巳晦，敕中書、門下與學士、諸王、駙馬入閣守歳，設庭燎，置酒，奏樂。

translations.literal: On dingsi, the last day of the month, the emperor ordered the Secretariat, Chancellery, academicians, various princes, and imperial sons-in-law to enter the pavilion to keep the year's vigil; court torches were set up, wine was laid out, and music was played.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, the last day of the month, the emperor summoned the Secretariat, Chancellery, academicians, princes, and imperial sons-in-law to the pavilion for the New Year's vigil; torches were lit in the courtyard, wine was served, and music was played.

sentences.zh: 酒酣，上謂御史大夫竇從一曰：「聞卿久無伉儷，朕毎憂之。

translations.literal: When the wine had warmed them, the emperor said to the Censor-in-Chief Dou Congyi: "I hear you have long had no spouse; I worry over this daily.
translations.idiomatic: As the wine flowed, the emperor said to Censor-in-Chief Dou Congyi: "I hear you have long been without a wife, and it has troubled me.

sentences.zh: 今夕歳除，爲卿成禮。」

translations.literal: Tonight, as the year is being put aside, I shall complete the rites for you."
translations.idiomatic: Tonight, as the old year ends, I shall arrange your wedding."

sentences.zh: 從一但唯唯拜謝。

translations.literal: Congyi could only murmur assent and bow in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Congyi murmured assent and bowed his thanks, unable to do otherwise.

sentences.zh: 俄而内侍引燭籠、歩障、金縷羅扇自西廊而上，扇後有人衣禮衣，花釵，令與從一對坐。

translations.literal: Presently inner attendants led candle lanterns, screen curtains, and gold-thread gauze fans up from the west corridor; behind the fans was someone in ceremonial dress with flowered hairpins, ordered to sit facing Congyi.
translations.idiomatic: Presently inner attendants escorted candle lanterns, screen curtains, and gilded gauze fans up from the west corridor; behind the fans stood a woman in bridal dress with flowered hairpins, who was seated facing Congyi.

sentences.zh: 上命從一誦《卻扇詩》數首。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Congyi to recite several stanzas of the "Removing the Fan" poem.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Congyi to recite several verses of the "Fan Withdrawn" ode.

sentences.zh: 扇卻，去花易服而出，徐視之，乃皇后老乳母王氏，本蠻婢也。

translations.literal: When the fan was withdrawn, she removed the flowers, changed clothes, and came forth; looking closely, it was the empress's aged wet nurse, Lady Wang—a barbarian slave girl by origin.
translations.idiomatic: When the fan was withdrawn, she removed her ornaments, changed clothes, and stepped forward; on closer look, she was the empress's aged wet nurse, Lady Wang—originally a barbarian serving girl.

sentences.zh: 上與侍臣大笑。

translations.literal: The emperor and the attending ministers roared with laughter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and his attending ministers burst into laughter.

sentences.zh: 詔封莒國夫人，嫁爲從一妻。

translations.literal: An edict enfeoffed her as Lady of the State of Ju and gave her in marriage as Congyi's wife.
translations.idiomatic: An edict enfeoffed her as Lady of Ju and gave her to Congyi in marriage.

sentences.zh: 俗謂乳母之婿曰：「阿沖」，從一毎謁見及進表狀，自稱「翊聖皇后阿沖」，時人謂之：「國沖」，從一欣然有自負之色。

translations.literal: Custom calls the son-in-law of a wet nurse "A-Chong"; whenever Congyi had audience or submitted memorials, he styled himself "A-Chong of the Empress of Assisting Sagacity"; people of the time called him "National Son-in-Law"—Congyi was pleased and showed a self-satisfied air.
translations.idiomatic: By custom a wet nurse's son-in-law was called "A-Chong"; whenever Congyi attended court or submitted memorials, he styled himself "A-Chong of the Empress of Assisting Sagacity." People called him "the Son-in-Law of the State," and Congyi wore a pleased, self-important air.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丁卯，制廣東都聖善寺，居民失業者數十家。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on dingmao, the emperor ordered the expansion of the Shengshan Temple in the eastern capital; several tens of households among the residents lost their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on dingmao, the emperor ordered the enlargement of Shengshan Temple in the eastern capital, displacing several dozen households from their homes and livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 長寧、安樂諸公主多縱僮奴掠百姓子女爲奴婢，侍御史袁從之收繫獄，治之。

translations.literal: The princesses of Changning, Anle, and others frequently allowed their pages and slaves to seize common people's sons and daughters as slaves; the attendant censor Yuan Congzhi arrested and imprisoned them and prosecuted the case.
translations.idiomatic: The Princesses of Changning and Anle, among others, often let their servants abduct commoners' children as slaves; attendant censor Yuan Congzhi arrested the offenders and prosecuted them.

sentences.zh: 公主訴於上，上手制釋之。

translations.literal: The princesses appealed to the emperor; the emperor wrote in his own hand an order releasing them.
translations.idiomatic: The princesses appealed to the emperor, who issued a personal edict ordering their release.

sentences.zh: 從之奏稱：「陛下縱奴掠良人，何以理天下！」

translations.literal: Congzhi memorialized: "Your Majesty indulges slaves in seizing good commoners—by what means can the realm be governed!"
translations.idiomatic: Congzhi memorialized: "If Your Majesty permits slaves to abduct free commoners, how can the realm be governed!"

sentences.zh: 上竟釋之。

translations.literal: The emperor released them after all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor released them anyway.

sentences.zh: 二月，己丑，上幸玄武門，與近臣觀宮女拔河。

translations.literal: In the second month, on jichou, the emperor visited the Xuanwu Gate and watched palace women tug-of-war with his close ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on jichou, the emperor went to the Xuanwu Gate with his close ministers to watch palace women compete at tug-of-war.

sentences.zh: 又命宮女爲市肆，公卿爲商旅，與之交易，因爲忿爭，言辭褻慢，上與後臨觀爲樂。

translations.literal: He also ordered palace women to set up market stalls, public ministers to play traveling merchants and trade with them—and because of quarrels, their words became vulgar and disrespectful; the emperor and empress watched from above and took it as amusement.
translations.idiomatic: He also had palace women run market stalls while ministers played traveling merchants and haggled with them; quarrels broke out in vulgar and disrespectful language, and the emperor and empress looked on with delight.

sentences.zh: 丙申，監察御史崔琬對仗彈宗楚客、紀處訥潛通戎狄，受其貨賂，致生邊患。

translations.literal: On bingshen, the supervising censor Cui Wan impeached at formal audience Zong Chuke and Ji Chuna for secretly communicating with frontier barbarians, accepting their bribes, and thereby causing border troubles.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, supervising censor Cui Wan impeached Zong Chuke and Ji Chuna at formal audience for secretly colluding with frontier tribes, taking their bribes, and thereby provoking border unrest.

sentences.zh: 故事，大臣被彈，俯僂趨出，立於朝堂待罪。

translations.literal: By precedent, when a great minister was impeached, he bowed low and hurried out to stand in the court hall awaiting judgment.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, when a senior minister was impeached, he bowed low, hurried from the hall, and stood in the outer court awaiting judgment.

sentences.zh: 至是，楚客更憤怒作色，自陳忠鯁，爲琬所誣。

translations.literal: On this occasion Chuke only grew angrier and changed color, declaring himself loyal and upright and that he was slandered by Wan.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion Chuke instead grew angry and flushed with rage, proclaiming his loyalty and declaring that Wan had slandered him.

sentences.zh: 上竟不窮問，命琬與楚客結爲兄弟以和解之，時人謂之「和事天子」。

translations.literal: The emperor ultimately did not pursue the matter to the end and ordered Wan and Chuke to become sworn brothers to reconcile them; people of the time called him "the Peacemaking Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor never pursued the matter and ordered Wan and Chuke to become sworn brothers to settle the dispute—people called him "the Peacemaking Emperor."

sentences.zh: 壬寅，以韋巨源爲左僕射，楊再思爲右僕射，並同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: On renyin, Wei Juyuan was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Yang Zaisi Right Vice Director, both concurrently Fellows of the Third Rank of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Wei Juyuan was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Yang Zaisi Right Vice Director, both with concurrent rank as Fellows of the Third Rank of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 上數與近臣學士宴集，令各效伎藝以爲樂。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly feasted with close ministers and academicians, ordering each to display his art as entertainment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor frequently held banquets with close ministers and academicians, ordering each to perform his special skill for amusement.

sentences.zh: 工部尚書張錫舞《談容娘》，將作大匠宗晉卿舞《渾脱》，左衞將軍張洽舞《黃獐》，左金吾將軍杜元談誦《婆羅門咒》，中書舍人盧藏用效道士上章。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Zhang Xi danced "Tanrongniang," Master Builder of the Imperial Works Zong Jinqing danced "Huntuo," General of the Left Guard Zhang Qia danced "Yellow Boar," General of the Left Golden Guard Du Yuanyan chanted the "Brahmin Spell," and Secretariat Drafting Officer Lu Zangyong performed a Daoist priest's petition to heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Zhang Xi danced "Tan Rongniang," Master Builder Zong Jinqing danced "Huntuo," General of the Left Guard Zhang Qia danced "Yellow Boar," General of the Left Golden Guard Du Yuanyan recited the Brahmin incantation, and Secretariat Drafting Officer Lu Zangyong mimicked a Daoist priest submitting a memorial to heaven.

sentences.zh: 國子司業河東郭山惲獨曰：「臣無所解，請歌古詩。」

translations.literal: The Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, Guo Shanyun of Hedong, alone said: "Your servant has no skill to display; I beg to sing ancient poetry."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Directorate of Education Guo Shanyun of Hedong alone said: "I have no talent to display; I ask instead to sing verses from the Classics."

sentences.zh: 上許之。

translations.literal: The emperor permitted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted his request.

sentences.zh: 山惲乃歌《鹿鳴》、《蟋蟀》。

translations.literal: Shanyun then sang "Deer Call" and "Cricket."
translations.idiomatic: Shanyun sang the "Deer Call" and "Cricket" odes from the Book of Songs.

sentences.zh: 明日，上賜山惲敕，嘉美其意，賜時服一襲。

translations.literal: The next day the emperor bestowed on Shanyun an edict praising his intent and gave him one set of contemporary dress.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor issued an edict praising Shanyun's intent and granted him a suit of court dress.

sentences.zh: 上又嘗宴侍臣，使各爲《回波辭》。

translations.literal: The emperor also once feasted his attending ministers and had each compose a "Rippling Wave" verse.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion the emperor feasted his ministers and had each compose a "Rippling Wave" verse.

sentences.zh: 衆皆爲諂語，或自求榮祿。

translations.literal: The multitude all made flattering words, or sought rank and salary for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The others all wrote flattery, or used the occasion to seek rank and emolument for themselves.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫李景伯曰：「回波爾時酒-{巵}-。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Counselor Li Jingbo said: "Rippling wave—in that hour, wine in the wine cup.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Counselor Li Jingbo said: "Rippling wave—in that hour, fill the wine cup.

sentences.zh: 微臣職在箴規。

translations.literal: Your humble servant's office lies in admonition and rule.
translations.idiomatic: This humble official's duty is to admonish and counsel.

sentences.zh: 侍宴既過三爵，喧嘩竊恐非儀。」

translations.literal: Attending a banquet already past three rounds of wine, the clamor I secretly fear is not ritual propriety."
translations.idiomatic: After three rounds at a banquet, such noisy revelry, I fear, falls short of proper decorum."

sentences.zh: 上不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's face darkened.

sentences.zh: 蕭至忠曰：「此眞諫官也。」

translations.literal: Xiao Zhizhong said: "This is a true remonstrating official."
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zhizhong said: "Here is a true remonstrating official.

sentences.zh: 三月，戊午，以宗楚客爲中書令，蕭至忠爲侍中，大府卿韋嗣立爲中書侍郎、同中書門下三品，中書侍郎崔湜、趙彦昭並同平章事。

translations.literal: In the third month, on wuwu, Zong Chuke was made Grand Counselor of the Secretariat, Xiao Zhizhong Palace Attendant, Grand Provisioner Wei Sili Secretariat Vice Minister and Fellow of the Third Rank of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and Secretariat Vice Ministers Cui Shi and Zhao Yanzhao both Equally Directors of Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on wuwu, Zong Chuke was appointed Grand Counselor of the Secretariat, Xiao Zhizhong Palace Attendant, Grand Provisioner Wei Sili Secretariat Vice Minister with concurrent rank as Fellow of the Third Rank, and Secretariat Vice Ministers Cui Shi and Zhao Yanzhao both as Equally Participating in Affairs.

sentences.zh: 崔湜通於上官昭容，故昭容引以爲相。

translations.literal: Cui Shi had relations with Brilliant Lady Shangguan; therefore the Brilliant Lady brought him in as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Shi was intimate with Brilliant Lady Shangguan, and it was she who brought him into the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 彦昭，張掖人也。

translations.literal: Yanzhao was a man of Zhangye.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhao was a native of Zhangye.

sentences.zh: 時政出多門，濫官充溢，人以爲三無坐處，謂宰相、御史及員外官也。

translations.literal: At the time government issued from many gates, spurious offices overflowed, and people said there were three kinds with nowhere to sit—meaning chancellors, censors, and supplementary officials.
translations.idiomatic: At the time power issued from many hands, offices were bloated with appointees, and people joked that three groups had nowhere to sit—the chancellors, the censors, and the supplementary officials.

sentences.zh: 韋嗣立上疎，以爲：「比者造寺極多，務取崇麗，大則用錢百數十萬，小則三五萬，無慮所費千萬以上，人力勞弊，怨嗟盈路。

translations.literal: Wei Sili submitted a memorial, stating: "Recently temple-building has been extremely numerous, striving for grandeur and splendor—large ones costing several millions of cash, small ones thirty or fifty thousand; the expenditure doubtless exceeds ten million altogether; laborers are worn and exhausted, and complaints fill the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sili submitted a memorial arguing: "Of late temple construction has proliferated, each striving for grandeur—large projects costing millions of cash, small ones thirty or fifty thousand; total expenditure surely exceeds ten million; laborers are exhausted, and grievances fill the roads.

sentences.zh: 佛之爲數，要在降伏身心，豈雕畫土木，相誇壯麗！

translations.literal: The purpose of Buddhism lies in subduing body and mind—how could carved-painted earth and wood, each vying in magnificence, serve that end!
translations.idiomatic: The essence of Buddhism is to subdue body and mind—what has that to do with gilded timber and stone built up to impress one another!

sentences.zh: 萬一水旱爲災，戎狄構患，雖龍象如雲，將何救哉！

translations.literal: If by chance flood and drought become disasters and frontier barbarians stir up trouble—though dragon-elephants crowd like clouds, what rescue could there be!
translations.idiomatic: Should flood or drought strike, or barbarians stir up trouble on the frontier, what good would all those temples full of monks do!

sentences.zh: 又，食封之家，其數甚衆，昨問戸部，雲用六十餘萬丁；

translations.literal: Moreover, households holding food-fiefs are extremely numerous; yesterday I asked the Ministry of Revenue, which said they employ more than six hundred thousand corvée men;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, recipients of food-fiefs are exceedingly numerous; I recently asked the Ministry of Revenue, which reported that they consume the labor of more than six hundred thousand corvée men;

sentences.zh: 一丁絹兩匹，凡百二十餘萬匹。

translations.literal: For each corvée man two bolts of silk—a total of more than 1.2 million bolts.
translations.idiomatic: At two bolts of silk per corvée man, that comes to more than 1.2 million bolts in all.

sentences.zh: 臣頃在太府，毎歳庸絹，多不過百萬，少則六七十萬匹，比之封家，所入殊少。

translations.literal: Your servant was recently at the Grand Treasury; each year's corvée silk was mostly no more than one million bolts, and at least six or seven hundred thousand—compared with the fief-holders, the state's intake is far smaller.
translations.idiomatic: When I served at the Grand Treasury, annual corvée silk rarely exceeded one million bolts and sometimes fell to six or seven hundred thousand—a fraction of what the fief-holders receive.

sentences.zh: 夫有佐命之勳，始可分茅胙土。

translations.literal: Only those with merit in assisting the mandate may begin to receive feudal fiefs and sacrificial lands.
translations.idiomatic: Only those who aided in founding the dynasty should receive territorial fiefs.

sentences.zh: 國初，功臣食封者不過三二十家，今以恩澤食封者乃逾百數；

translations.literal: At the dynasty's founding, meritorious ministers holding food-fiefs were no more than twenty or thirty households; now those holding food-fiefs through grace and favor exceed one hundred in number;
translations.idiomatic: At the dynasty's founding, no more than twenty or thirty meritorious ministers held food-fiefs; now those granted fiefs through imperial favor exceed one hundred.

sentences.zh: 國家租賦，太半私門，私門有餘，徒益奢侈，公家不足，坐致憂危，制國之方，豈謂爲得！

translations.literal: The state's land tax and levies—more than half go to private houses; private houses have surplus and only increase extravagance; the public coffers are insufficient and thereby invite anxiety and peril—could this way of ordering the state be called right!
translations.idiomatic: More than half the state's tax revenue flows into private hands; the wealthy grow more extravagant while the treasury runs dry, inviting crisis—is this any way to govern a realm!

sentences.zh: 封戸之物，諸家自征，僮僕依勢，陵轢州縣，多索裹頭，轉行貿易，煩擾驅迫，不勝其苦。

translations.literal: As for goods from fief households, each family collects them itself; servants rely on power, bully and overrun prefectures and counties, demand much in head-wrapping fees, carry on trade, harass and drive and compel—people cannot bear the suffering.
translations.idiomatic: Each fief-holding family collects its own tribute in person; their servants, abusing their masters' status, bully local officials, extort fees under every pretext, and engage in trade on the side—harassing and coercing the populace until the people can endure no more.

sentences.zh: 不若悉計丁輸之太府，使封家於左藏受之，於事爲愈。

translations.literal: It would be better to calculate by adult males and remit all to the Grand Treasury, letting fief-holding families receive payment at the Left Storehouse—in affairs this would be preferable.
