translations.idiomatic: Better to levy by head count, remit everything to the central treasury, and let fief holders draw their allotments from the imperial coffers—that would be far less disruptive.

sentences.zh: 又，員外置官，數倍正闕，曹署典吏，困於祗承，府庫倉儲，竭於資奉。

translations.literal: Again, supernumerary appointments are several times the regular vacancies; clerks in bureau offices are worn out by attendance and service; treasuries and granaries are drained by supporting salaries.
translations.idiomatic: Supernumerary officials outnumber regular posts several times over; clerks in every bureau are exhausted keeping up with them, and the treasury and granaries are drained dry paying their salaries.

sentences.zh: 又，刺史、縣令，近年以來，不存簡擇，京官有犯及聲望下者方遣刺州，吏部選人，衰耄無手筆者方補縣令。

translations.literal: Again, for prefects and county magistrates, in recent years no care is taken in selection; only when capital officials have committed offenses or have low repute are they sent to govern prefectures; from the Ministry of Personnel's selectees, only the decrepit and aged without literary talent are appointed as county magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years no care has been taken in choosing prefects and county magistrates—disgraced or second-rate capital officials are dispatched to govern provinces, while the Ministry of Personnel fills county posts with senile men who can barely wield a brush.

sentences.zh: 以此理人，何由率化！

translations.literal: Using this to govern people—how can one lead transformation!
translations.idiomatic: With such men administering the realm, how can good order ever take hold!

sentences.zh: 望自今應除三省、兩台及五品以上淸望官，皆先於刺史、縣令中選用，則天下理矣。」

translations.literal: I hope that from now on, for all appointments to the Three Departments, Two Chancelleries, and prestigious posts of fifth rank and above, one may first select from among prefects and county magistrates—then All-under-Heaven will be well governed."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, when filling posts in the Three Departments, the Two Chancelleries, and other prestigious offices of fifth rank or higher, Your Majesty should first promote proven prefects and magistrates—that alone would set the realm aright."

sentences.zh: 上弗聽。

translations.literal: The emperor did not heed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor declined to listen.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，以禮部尚書韋温爲太子少保、同中書門下三品，太常卿鄭愔爲吏部尚書、同平章事。

translations.literal: On wuyin, Wei Wen, Minister of Rites, was made Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent and given the rank of Concurrent Associate of the Secretariat-Chancellery of the Third Rank; Zheng Yin, Director of Ceremonies, was made Minister of Personnel and made Concurrent Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Minister of Rites Wei Wen was appointed Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent with concurrent rank as Associate of the Secretariat-Chancellery of the Third Rank; Director of Ceremonies Zheng Yin was appointed Minister of Personnel and Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 温，皇后之兄也。

translations.literal: Wen was the empress's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Wen was the empress's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 太常博士唐紹以武氏昊陵、順陵置守戸五百，與昭陵數同，梁宣王、魯忠王墓守戸多於親王五倍，韋氏褒德廟衞兵多於太廟，上疎請量裁減；

translations.literal: Grand Master of Sacrifices Tang Shao submitted that the Wu clan's Haoling and Shunling had five hundred guard households assigned, the same number as Zhaoling; the tombs of the Prince of Liang Xuan and the Prince of Lu Zhong had guard households five times those of imperial princes; the guard troops of the Wei clan's Baode Temple exceeded those of the Grand Ancestral Temple—he memorialized requesting measured reduction according to circumstances;
translations.idiomatic: Tang Shao, a Grand Master of Sacrifices, submitted that the Wu tombs at Haoling and Shunling each had five hundred guard households—the same allotment as Emperor Taizong's Zhaoling; the tombs of the Prince of Liang Xuan and the Prince of Lu Zhong had five times as many as any imperial prince; and the Wei clan's Baode Temple had more guard troops than the Grand Ancestral Temple itself. He urged the emperor to cut these allotments proportionally;

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor did not heed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 紹，臨之孫也。

translations.literal: Shao was Lin's grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Shao was the grandson of Tang Lin.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎兼知吏部侍郎、同平章事崔湜、吏部侍郎同平章事鄭愔倶掌銓衡，傾附勢要，贓賄狼藉，數外留人，授擬不中，逆用三年闕，選法大壞。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Secretariat and acting Vice Minister of Personnel, Concurrent Grand Counselor Cui Shi, and Vice Minister of Personnel, Concurrent Grand Counselor Zheng Yin, together controlled the balance of selection; they leaned toward the powerful and influential, bribery lay scattered everywhere, they repeatedly retained men beyond quota, their appointment drafts missed the mark, they perversely used three years' worth of vacancies—the selection laws were greatly ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Shi, Vice Director of the Secretariat who also served as acting Vice Minister of Personnel and Grand Counselor, and Zheng Yin, Vice Minister of Personnel and Grand Counselor, jointly controlled official appointments—favoring the powerful, taking bribes openly, holding back positions to sell, botching every recommendation, and recklessly drawing on three years' worth of vacancies. The civil service examination system was utterly corrupt.

sentences.zh: 湜父挹爲司業，受選人錢，湜不之知，長名放之。

translations.literal: Shi's father Yi served as Vice Director of the Directorate of Education; he accepted money from selectees—Shi did not know of it and passed him on the long list.
translations.idiomatic: Shi's father Yi, serving as Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, had taken a bribe from an examinee; Shi, unaware of the transaction, approved the man's appointment on the final roster.

sentences.zh: 其人訴曰：「公所親受某賂，奈何不與官？」

translations.literal: That man pleaded, saying: 'Your close associate took a bribe from me—why will you not grant me an office?"
translations.idiomatic: The man protested: 'One of your intimates accepted a bribe from me—why won't you grant me a post?"

sentences.zh: 湜怒曰：「所親爲誰，當擒取杖殺之！」

translations.literal: Shi angrily said: 'Who is this close associate? He should be seized and beaten to death with staves!"
translations.idiomatic: Shi flew into a rage: 'Name this intimate of mine—I shall have him seized and beaten to death!"

sentences.zh: 其人曰：「公勿杖殺，將使公遭憂。」

translations.literal: The man said: 'Do not beat him to death—it will bring grief upon you, sir."
translations.idiomatic: The man replied: 'Don't beat him to death, sir—you'll only bring trouble on yourself."

sentences.zh: 湜大慚。

translations.literal: Shi was greatly ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was deeply mortified.

sentences.zh: 侍御史勒恆與監察御史李尚隱對仗彈之，上下湜等獄，命監察御史裴漼按之。

translations.literal: Attendant Censor Le Heng and Investigating Censor Li Shangyin impeached them facing the throne in court session; Shi and the others were put into prison above and below, and Investigating Censor Pei Hui was ordered to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Censor Le Heng and Investigating Censor Li Shangyin impeached them before the throne; Cui Shi and his associates were imprisoned, and Investigating Censor Pei Hui was ordered to conduct the inquiry.

sentences.zh: 安樂公主諷漼寬其獄，漼復對仗彈之。

translations.literal: Princess Anle hinted to Hui to lighten their case; Hui again impeached them facing the throne in court session.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Anle pressured Pei Hui to leniently handle the case; he responded by impeaching the conspirators again before the throne.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，丙寅，愔免死，流吉州，湜貶江州司馬。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on bingyin, Yin was spared death and exiled to Jizhou; Shi was demoted to Army Vice Marshal of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, on bingyin, Zheng Yin was spared execution and exiled to Jizhou; Cui Shi was demoted to vice marshal of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 上官昭容密與安樂公主、武延秀曲爲申理，明日，以湜爲襄州刺史，愔爲江州司馬。

translations.literal: Shangguan Zhaorong secretly joined Princess Anle and Wu Yanxiu in bending arguments to plead their case; the next day, Shi was made Prefect of Xiangzhou and Yin was made Army Vice Marshal of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shangguan Zhaorong secretly colluded with Princess Anle and Wu Yanxiu to plead their case; the very next day Cui Shi was appointed prefect of Xiangzhou and Zheng Yin was made vice marshal of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 六月，右僕射、同中書門下三品楊再思薨。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Right Vice Premier, Concurrent Associate of the Secretariat-Chancellery of the Third Rank Yang Zaisi died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Right Vice Premier Yang Zaisi, concurrent Associate of the Secretariat-Chancellery of the Third Rank, died.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，突騎施娑葛遣使請降；

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Soge of the Turgesh sent envoys requesting surrender;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Soge of the Turgesh sent envoys to submit;

sentences.zh: 庚辰，拜欽化可汗，賜名守忠。

translations.literal: On gengchen, he was invested as Qinhua Qaghan and given the name Shouzhong.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen he was invested as Qinhua Qaghan and given the name Shouzhong.

sentences.zh: 八月，己酉，以李嶠同中書門下三品，韋安石爲侍中，蕭至忠爲中書令。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on jiyou, Li Qiao was made Concurrent Associate of the Secretariat-Chancellery of the Third Rank; Wei Anshi was made Palace Attendant; Xiao Zhizhong was made Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on jiyou, Li Qiao was made Associate of the Secretariat-Chancellery of the Third Rank; Wei Anshi was appointed Palace Attendant; Xiao Zhizhong was made Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 至忠女適皇后舅子崔無諳，成昏日，上主蕭氏，後主崔氏，時人謂之「天子嫁女，皇后娶婦」。

translations.literal: Zhizhong's daughter was married to the empress's nephew's son Cui Wuyin; on the wedding day, the emperor presided over the Xiao family and the empress presided over the Cui family—people of the time called it 'the Son of Heaven marrying off a daughter, the empress taking a daughter-in-law.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong's daughter married Cui Wuyin, the empress's nephew; at the wedding the emperor presided over the Xiao family's rites while the empress presided over the Cui family's. Contemporaries quipped that it was 'the Son of Heaven giving away a bride while the empress took one in.'

sentences.zh: 上將祀南郊，丁酉，國子祭酒祝欽明、國子司業郭山惲建言：「古者大祭祀，後裸獻以瑤爵。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to sacrifice at the Southern Altar; on dingyou, Libationer of the Directorate of Education Zhu Qinming and Vice Director Guo Shanyun proposed: 'In antiquity at great sacrifices, the empress performed the unclothed offering and presented with a jade cup.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor prepared to sacrifice at the Southern Altar, on dingyou Libationer Zhu Qinming and Vice Director Guo Shanyun of the Directorate of Education proposed: 'In antiquity, at the great sacrifice the empress performed the unvested offering and presented libations with a jade cup.

sentences.zh: 皇后當助祭天地。」

translations.literal: The empress ought to assist in sacrificing to Heaven and Earth."
translations.idiomatic: The empress should assist in sacrificing to Heaven and Earth."

sentences.zh: 太常博士唐紹、蔣欽緒駁之，以爲：「鄭玄注《周禮‧内司服》，惟有助祭先王先公，無助祭天地之文。

translations.literal: Grand Masters of Sacrifices Tang Shao and Jiang Qinxu rebutted them, holding: 'In Zheng Xuan's commentary on the Internal Minister of Attire section of the Rites of Zhou, there is only assisting sacrifice to former kings and former lords—there is no text on assisting sacrifice to Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Masters of Sacrifices Tang Shao and Jiang Qinxu objected, arguing: 'In Zheng Xuan's commentary on the Internal Minister of Attire in the Rites of Zhou, empresses assist only at sacrifices to royal ancestors—nowhere does the text mention assisting at sacrifices to Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 皇后不當助祭南郊。」

translations.literal: The empress ought not assist in sacrificing at the Southern Suburb."
translations.idiomatic: The empress has no place assisting at the Southern Altar sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 國子司業鹽官褚無量議。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, Yanguan man Chu Wuliang offered his opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Chu Wuliang of Yanguan also weighed in.

sentences.zh: 以爲：「祭天惟以始祖爲主，不配以祖妣，故皇后不應預祭。」

translations.literal: He held: 'When sacrificing to Heaven, only the founding ancestor is taken as chief; ancestors and ancestresses are not paired—therefore the empress ought not participate in the sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: He argued: 'Heaven is worshipped with the founding ancestor alone, without pairing an ancestress—therefore the empress should not take part."

sentences.zh: 韋巨源定儀注，請依欽明議。

translations.literal: Wei Juyuan fixed the ritual regulations and requested following Qinming's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Juyuan drafted the ritual protocol and sided with Qinming's proposal.

sentences.zh: 上從之，以皇后爲亞獻，仍以宰相女爲齋娘，助執豆籩。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this; the empress was made secondary offerer, and moreover daughters of chancellors were made fasting maidens to assist in holding the bean dishes and baskets.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, appointing the empress as secondary offerer and selecting daughters of chancellors as fasting maidens to assist in presenting the ritual vessels.

sentences.zh: 欽明又欲以安樂公主爲終獻，紹、欽緒固爭，乃止；

translations.literal: Qinming further wished to make Princess Anle the final offerer; Shao and Qinxu firmly contested this, and it was stopped;
translations.idiomatic: Qinming then proposed making Princess Anle the final offerer; Shao and Qinxu strenuously objected, and the idea was dropped;

sentences.zh: 以巨源攝太尉爲終獻。

translations.literal: Juyuan, acting as Grand Marshal, served as final offerer.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Juyuan, acting as Grand Marshal, performed the final offering instead.

sentences.zh: 欽緒，膠水人也。

translations.literal: Qinxu was a man of Jiaoshui.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Qinxu was a native of Jiaoshui.

sentences.zh: 己巳，上幸定昆池，命從官賦詩。

translations.literal: On jisi, the emperor visited Dingkun Pool and ordered his attendant officials to compose poems.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi the emperor visited Dingkun Pool and ordered his courtiers to compose poems.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎李日知詩曰：「所願暫思居者逸，勿使時稱作者勞。」

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Yellow Gate Li Rizhi's poem said: 'My wish is briefly to reflect that those who dwell at ease should rest—do not let the age say that writers of verse suffer toil."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Yellow Gate Li Rizhi wrote: 'Let those at leisure enjoy their ease for a time—do not let the age praise poets for their labors.'

sentences.zh: 及睿宗即位，謂日知曰：「當是時，朕亦不敢言之。」

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, he said to Rizhi: 'At that time, I too did not dare speak such words."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong later took the throne, he told Rizhi: 'Even I would not have dared say that at the time.'

sentences.zh: 九月，戊辰，以蘇瑰爲右僕射、同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on wuchen, Su Gui was made Right Vice Premier and Concurrent Associate of the Secretariat-Chancellery of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on wuchen, Su Gui was appointed Right Vice Premier with concurrent rank as Associate of the Secretariat-Chancellery of the Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 太平、安樂公主各樹朋黨，更相譖毀，上患之。

translations.literal: Princess Taiping and Princess Anle each built factions of partisans and mutually slandered and reviled each other; the emperor was troubled by this.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Taiping and Princess Anle each assembled rival factions and continually slandered one another; the emperor was deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，癸亥，上謂修文館直學士武平一曰：「比聞内外親貴多不輯睦，以何法和之？」

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, on guihai, the emperor said to Xiuzhiwen Hall Direct Academician Wu Pingyi: 'I have lately heard that close kin and the nobility within and without are mostly not harmonious—by what method can they be reconciled?"
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, on guihai, the emperor said to Direct Academician Wu Pingyi of the Xiuzhiwen Hall: 'I hear that the imperial kin and nobility, inside and outside the palace, are scarcely on speaking terms—what can be done to restore harmony?"

sentences.zh: 平一以爲：「此由讒諂之人陰爲離間，宜深加誨諭，斥逐奸險。

translations.literal: Pingyi held: 'This comes from slanderous and fawning men secretly causing division—it is fitting to instruct them deeply and expel the wicked and treacherous.
translations.idiomatic: Pingyi replied: 'Slanderers and flatterers are driving them apart from behind the scenes. Your Majesty should counsel them firmly and drive out the wicked and treacherous.

sentences.zh: 若猶未已，伏願捨近圖遠，抑慈存嚴，示以知禁，無令積惡。」

translations.literal: If still it does not stop, I humbly wish to set aside the near and plan for the far, restrain kindness and preserve severity, show them that transgression is forbidden, and not let wickedness accumulate."
translations.idiomatic: If that fails, Your Majesty must look beyond family ties, temper mercy with severity, and make clear that certain lines must not be crossed—before the evil grows beyond remedy."

sentences.zh: 上賜平一帛，而不能用其言。

translations.literal: The emperor bestowed silk on Pingyi but could not employ his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rewarded him with silk but did nothing with his advice.

sentences.zh: 上召前修文館學士崔湜、鄭愔入陪大禮。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned former Xiuzhiwen Hall Academicians Cui Shi and Zheng Yin to attend the great ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned former Xiuzhiwen Hall academicians Cui Shi and Zheng Yin to attend the great sacrificial rite.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，上祀南郊，赦天下，並十惡鹹赦除之；

translations.literal: On yichou, the emperor sacrificed at the Southern Suburb, proclaimed amnesty throughout All-under-Heaven, and pardoned even the ten abominations completely;
translations.idiomatic: On yichou the emperor sacrificed at the Southern Altar, proclaimed a general amnesty—even the ten capital offenses were forgiven;

sentences.zh: 流人並放還；

translations.literal: exiles were all released and sent back;
translations.idiomatic: exiles were recalled;

sentences.zh: 齋娘有婿者，皆改官。

translations.literal: fasting maidens who had husbands were all given new official posts.
translations.idiomatic: and husbands of the fasting maidens were all given official appointments.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，開府儀同三司、平章軍國重事豆盧欽望薨。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Grand General of the State with Preamble, Grand Counselor for Military and State Affairs Doulu Qinwang died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Doulu Qinwang, Grand General of the State with Preamble and Grand Counselor for Military and State Affairs, died.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，吐蕃贊普遣其大臣尚贊咄等千餘人逆金城公主。

translations.literal: On yihai, the Tibetan Btsan-po sent his ministers Shang Zhanzhu and more than a thousand others to meet Princess Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai the Tibetan king sent over a thousand men led by his minister Shang Zhanzhu to escort Princess Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 河南道巡察使、監察御史宋務光，以「於時食實封者凡一百四十餘家，應出封戸者凡五十四州，皆割上腴之田，或一封分食數州；

translations.literal: Henan Circuit Touring Commissioner and Investigating Censor Song Wuguang submitted: 'At this time those holding substantive fiefs totaled more than one hundred forty households; those obliged to supply fief households totaled fifty-four prefectures—all cut off the richest fields, or one fief shared food across several prefectures;
translations.idiomatic: Song Wuguang, Henan Circuit Touring Commissioner and Investigating Censor, submitted: 'More than one hundred forty households now hold substantive fiefs, drawing tribute from fifty-four prefectures—each staking claim to the richest land, some single fiefs feeding across several provinces;

sentences.zh: 而太平、安樂公主又取髙資多丁者，刻剝過苦，應充封戸者甚於征役；

translations.literal: moreover Princess Taiping and Princess Anle further took those of high assets and many adult males—their extortion excessively bitter; those obliged to serve as fief households suffered worse than conscript labor;
translations.idiomatic: Princess Taiping and Princess Anle moreover seize the wealthiest districts with the largest populations, extracting tribute so ruthlessly that serving as fief households is worse than conscription;

sentences.zh: 滑州地出綾縑，人多趨射，尤受其弊，人多流亡；

translations.literal: Huazhou's land produces damask and fine silk; many people rush to seek fief allotments and especially suffer this harm—many people become exiles;
translations.idiomatic: Huazhou, famed for its silks, draws crowds seeking fief allotments and suffers worst of all—its people flee in droves;

sentences.zh: 請稍分封戸散配餘州。

translations.literal: I request slightly dividing fief households and scattering allocation among the remaining prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: I urge that fief households be distributed more evenly across the remaining prefectures.

sentences.zh: 又，征封使者煩擾公私，請附租庸，毎年送納。」

translations.literal: Again, fief-collection envoys harass public and private alike—I request attaching collection to the land tax and corvée payments, remitted each year."
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, the envoys who collect fief tribute harass officials and commoners alike—I urge that fief payments be folded into the regular land tax and delivered annually."

sentences.zh: 上弗聽。

translations.literal: The emperor did not heed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 時流人皆放還，均州刺史譙王重福獨不得歸，乃上表自陳曰：「陛下焚柴展禮，郊祀上玄，蒼生並得赦除，赤子偏加擯棄，皇天平分之道，固若此乎！

translations.literal: At this time exiles were all released and sent back; only Prince Qiao Zhongfu, Prefect of Junzhou, could not return home, and so he submitted a memorial stating himself: 'Your Majesty burned firewood and extended the rites, performed suburban sacrifice to the Supreme Mystery—all living beings alike received pardon and release, yet this humble child is specially added to rejection and abandonment—is the Way of Heaven's fair allotment truly like this!
translations.idiomatic: Though all exiles were recalled, Prince Qiao Zhongfu, prefect of Junzhou, alone was denied permission to return. He submitted a memorial: 'Your Majesty has burned the firewood and performed the suburban sacrifice to Heaven—all the common people have been pardoned, yet I alone am cast aside. Is this what Heaven's justice looks like!

sentences.zh: 天下之人聞者爲臣流涕。

translations.literal: All people under Heaven who heard wept tears for me.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard my plea wept for me.

sentences.zh: 況陛下慈念，豈不愍臣棲遑！」

translations.literal: Moreover Your Majesty's compassionate thoughts—would you not pity my anxious wandering!"
translations.idiomatic: Surely Your Majesty's compassion cannot leave me wandering in despair!"

sentences.zh: 表奏，不報。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; no reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: No answer came.

sentences.zh: 前右僕射致仕唐休璟，年八十餘，進取彌鋭，娶賀婁尚宮養女爲其子婦。

translations.literal: Former Right Vice Premier, retired Tang Xiujing, aged more than eighty, his quest for advancement grew sharper; he took Palace Lady Helou's foster daughter as his son's wife.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Xiujing, the retired former Right Vice Premier, was past eighty yet as ambitious as ever—he arranged for his son to marry the foster daughter of Palace Lady Helou.

sentences.zh: 十二月，壬辰，以休璟爲太子少師、同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on renchen, Xiujing was made Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent and Concurrent Associate of the Secretariat-Chancellery of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on renchen, Tang Xiujing was appointed Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent with concurrent rank as Associate of the Secretariat-Chancellery of the Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 甲午，上幸驪山温湯；

translations.literal: On jiawu, the emperor visited the hot springs at Mount Li;
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu the emperor visited the hot springs at Mount Li;

sentences.zh: 庚子，幸韋嗣立莊捨。

translations.literal: on gengzi, he visited Wei Silie's estate lodge.
translations.idiomatic: on gengzi he visited the estate lodge of Wei Silie.

sentences.zh: 以嗣立與周髙士韋□同族，賜爵逍遙公。

translations.literal: Because Silie was of the same clan as the Zhou eminent Wei □, he was granted the title Duke of Xiaoyao.
translations.idiomatic: Because Silie claimed kinship with the Zhou dynasty worthy Wei □, the emperor bestowed on him the title Duke of Free Roaming.

sentences.zh: 嗣立，皇后之疎屬也。

translations.literal: Silie was a distant kinsman of the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Silie was a distant relation of the empress.

sentences.zh: 由是顧賞尤重。

translations.literal: From this his royal favor and rewards were especially heavy.
translations.idiomatic: From that point the emperor showered him with especially lavish favor.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，還宮。

translations.literal: On yisi, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi the emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 是歳，關中饑，米斗百錢。

translations.literal: This year, Guanzhong suffered famine; a dou of rice cost one hundred cash.
translations.idiomatic: That year famine struck Guanzhong; rice cost a hundred cash per dou.

sentences.zh: 運山東、江、淮谷輸京師，牛死什八九。

translations.literal: Grain from Shandong, the Yangtze, and the Huai was transported to the capital; oxen died eight or nine in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Grain was shipped from Shandong and the Yangtze-Huai region to the capital; eight or nine out of every ten oxen died on the road.

sentences.zh: 群臣多請車駕復幸東都，韋後家本杜陵，不樂東遷，乃使巫覡彭君卿等説上云：「今歳不利東行。」

translations.literal: Many among the ministers requested that the imperial carriage again visit the Eastern Capital; Empress Wei's family was originally from Duling and did not rejoice in moving east, and so sent shamans Peng Junqing and others to persuade the emperor, saying: 'This year is unfavorable for travel eastward."
translations.idiomatic: Many officials urged the emperor to relocate to the Eastern Capital; the empress, whose family hailed from Duling near Chang'an, resisted moving east and sent shamans including Peng Junqing to warn the emperor: 'This year is ill-omened for travel eastward."

sentences.zh: 後復有言者，上怒曰：「豈有逐糧天子邪！」

translations.literal: Later when others again spoke of it, the emperor angrily said: 'Can there be an emperor who chases after grain!"
translations.idiomatic: When others raised the subject again, the emperor raged: 'Am I an emperor who flees his capital for a sack of grain!"

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: And so it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 睿宗玄眞大聖大興孝皇帝上

translations.literal: Above: Emperor Ruizong, the Profound and True Great Sage, Great Promoter of Filial Piety
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ruizong the Profound and True Great Sage, Great Promoter of Filial Piety — Part One

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丙寅夜，中宗與韋後微行觀燈於市裡，又縱宮女數千人出遊，多不歸者。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the night of bingyin, Emperor Zhongzong and Empress Wei went incognito to view lanterns in the marketplace; moreover he released several thousand palace women to go out sightseeing—many did not return.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the night of bingyin, Emperor Zhongzong and Empress Wei slipped out incognito to view the festival lanterns in the marketplace; he also released several thousand palace women to go sightseeing—many never returned.

sentences.zh: 上命紀處訥送金城公主適吐蕃，處訥辭；

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Ji Chune to escort Princess Jincheng in marriage to Tibet; Chune declined;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Ji Chune to escort Princess Jincheng to Tibet for her marriage; Chune refused;

sentences.zh: 又命趙彦昭，彦昭亦辭。

translations.literal: he then ordered Zhao Yanzhao, and Yanzhao also declined.
translations.idiomatic: he then ordered Zhao Yanzhao, who also refused.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，命左驍衞大將軍楊矩送之。

translations.literal: On dingchou, he ordered Left Brave Guard General Yang Ju to escort her.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou he appointed Left Brave Guard General Yang Ju to escort her.

sentences.zh: 己卯，上自送公主至始平；

translations.literal: On jimao, the emperor personally escorted the princess as far as Shiping;
translations.idiomatic: On jimao the emperor personally escorted the princess as far as Shiping;

sentences.zh: 二月，癸未，還宮。

translations.literal: in the second month, on guiwei, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: in the second month, on guiwei, he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 公主至吐蕃，贊普爲之別築城以居之。

translations.literal: When the princess reached Tibet, the Btsan-po built a separate city for her to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: When the princess reached Tibet, the king built a separate city for her residence.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，上御梨園毯塲，命文武三品以上抛毯及分朋拔河。

translations.literal: On gengxu, the emperor attended the Pear Garden ball ground and ordered civil and military officials of third rank and above to toss the ball and form sides for tug-of-war.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu the emperor presided at the Pear Garden ball ground, ordering civil and military officials of third rank and above to play cuju and divide into teams for tug-of-war.

sentences.zh: 韋巨源、唐休璟衰老，隨絲亙踣地，久之不能興；

translations.literal: Wei Juyuan and Tang Xiujing, aged and decrepit, followed the rope and fell to the ground together—long they could not rise;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Juyuan and Tang Xiujing, both elderly and frail, joined the tug-of-war, grabbed the rope, and toppled to the ground—they lay there unable to rise for a long while;

sentences.zh: 上及皇后、妃、主臨觀，大笑。

translations.literal: the emperor together with the empress, consorts, and princesses watched from nearby and laughed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor, empress, consorts, and princesses looked on and roared with laughter.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丙戌，上游芳林園，命公卿馬上摘櫻桃。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on bingxu, the emperor visited Fanglin Garden and ordered the high ministers on horseback to pick cherries.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on bingxu, the emperor visited Fanglin Garden and ordered his chief ministers to pick cherries from horseback.

sentences.zh: 初，則天之世，長安城東隅民王純家井溢，浸成大池數十頃，號隆慶池。

translations.literal: Initially, in Empress Wu's era, at the eastern corner of Chang'an city, commoner Wang Chun's family well overflowed and soaked into a great pool of several dozen qing, called Longqing Pool.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during Empress Wu's reign, a well in commoner Wang Chun's home at the eastern edge of Chang'an overflowed and spread into a lake of several dozen acres, called Longqing Pool.

sentences.zh: 相王子五王列第於其北，望氣者言：「常鬱鬱有帝王氣，比日尤甚。」

translations.literal: The five princes, sons of the former emperor, arrayed mansions to its north; a geomancer said: 'Perpetually overcast it has imperial qi; in recent days it is especially strong."
translations.idiomatic: The five princes had built their mansions along its northern shore; geomancers warned: 'An imperial aura broods over those waters—lately it has grown stronger still."

sentences.zh: 乙未，上幸隆慶池，結綵爲樓，宴侍臣，泛舟戲象以厭之。

translations.literal: On yiwei, the emperor visited Longqing Pool, constructed a tower of colored silk, feasted attendant ministers, and floated boats playing elephants to suppress it.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei the emperor visited Longqing Pool, erected a pavilion draped in colored silk, feasted his ministers, and launched boats with elephant performances to dispel the omen.

sentences.zh: 定州人郎岌上言：「韋後、宗楚客將爲逆亂。」

translations.literal: Lang Ji of Dingzhou submitted: 'Empress Wei and Zong Chuke are about to commit treason and rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: Lang Ji of Dingzhou submitted: 'Empress Wei and Zong Chuke are plotting rebellion."

sentences.zh: 韋後白上，杖殺之。

translations.literal: Empress Wei informed the emperor, and he was beaten to death with staves.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wei told the emperor, and Lang Ji was beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 五月，丁卯，許州司兵參軍偃師燕欽融復上言：「皇后淫亂，干預國政，宗族強盛；

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on dingmao, Yanshi man Yan Qinrong, Army Adjutant of Xuzhou, again submitted: 'The empress is licentious and dissolute, meddles in state affairs, and her clan is powerful and flourishing;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on dingmao, Yan Qinrong of Yanshi, Army Adjutant of Xuzhou, submitted again: 'The empress is corrupt and meddles in state affairs; her clan grows ever more powerful;

sentences.zh: 安樂公主、武延秀、宗楚客圖危宗社。」

translations.literal: Princess Anle, Wu Yanxiu, and Zong Chuke plot to endanger the ancestral temple and altars."
translations.idiomatic: Princess Anle, Wu Yanxiu, and Zong Chuke conspire against the dynasty itself."

sentences.zh: 上召欽融面詰之。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Qinrong to face him and interrogated him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Yan Qinrong and questioned him to his face.

sentences.zh: 欽融頓首抗言，神色不撓；

translations.literal: Qinrong bowed his head to the ground and spoke defiantly; his expression did not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Qinrong kowtowed but spoke without flinching, his face unmoved;

sentences.zh: 上默然。

translations.literal: the emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor fell silent.

sentences.zh: 宗楚客矯制令飛騎撲殺之，投於殿庭石上，折頸而死，楚客大呼稱快。

translations.literal: Zong Chuke forged an edict ordering Flying Cavalry to beat him to death; he was thrown onto the stone paving of the palace courtyard, his neck broken and he died; Chuke shouted loudly in satisfaction.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Chuke forged an imperial order and had the Flying Cavalry beat him to death, hurling his body onto the courtyard stones and breaking his neck; Chuke shouted with delight.

sentences.zh: 上雖不窮問，意頗怏怏不悅；

translations.literal: Although the emperor did not pursue the matter to the end, he was nonetheless quite displeased and unhappy;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not press the inquiry, but he was plainly displeased;

sentences.zh: 由是韋後及其黨始憂懼。

translations.literal: From this Empress Wei and her faction first began to worry and fear.
translations.idiomatic: From that point on, Empress Wei and her clique grew anxious and afraid.

sentences.zh: 己卯，上宴近臣，國子祭酒祝欽明自請作《八風舞》，搖頭轉目，備諸醜態；

translations.literal: On jimao, the emperor feasted his close ministers; Director of the Directorate of Education Zhu Qinming volunteered to perform the Dance of the Eight Winds, wagging his head and rolling his eyes, displaying every ugly manner;
translations.idiomatic: On jimao the emperor entertained his inner circle. Zhu Qinming, Director of the Directorate of Education, offered to perform the Dance of the Eight Winds, twisting his head and rolling his eyes in every grotesque pose imaginable;

sentences.zh: 上笑。

translations.literal: The emperor laughed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor burst out laughing.

sentences.zh: 欽明素以儒學著名，吏部侍郎盧藏用私謂諸學士曰：「祝公《五經》，掃地盡矣！」

translations.literal: Qinming had long been famed for Confucian learning; Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Lu Cangyong privately said to the academicians: "Master Zhu's Five Classics—swept clean to the last!"
translations.idiomatic: Qinming had built his reputation on Confucian scholarship; Lu Cangyong, Vice Minister of Personnel, whispered to the academicians: "Master Zhu has swept his reputation for the Five Classics straight into the dustbin!"

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍馬秦客以醫術，光祿少卿楊均以善烹調，皆出入宮掖，得幸於韋後，恐事洩被誅；

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary Ma Qinke for his medical skill, and Vice Director of the Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan Yang Jun for his skill in cooking, all went in and out of the inner palace, gained favor with Empress Wei, and feared that if the affair leaked they would be executed;
translations.idiomatic: Ma Qinke, Attendant-in-Ordinary, owed his access to medical expertise; Yang Jun, Vice Director of the Imperial Clan, to his gift for cuisine. Both moved freely in the inner palace, had won Empress Wei's favor, and feared execution if the plot were exposed.

sentences.zh: 安樂公主欲韋後臨朝，自爲皇太女；

translations.literal: Princess Anle wished Empress Wei to preside over court, and herself to become crown princess;
translations.idiomatic: Princess Anle wanted Empress Wei to rule from behind the curtain—and wanted to be named crown princess herself.

sentences.zh: 乃相與合謀，於餅餤中進毒。

translations.literal: Thereupon they together formed a conspiracy and introduced poison in cakes.
translations.idiomatic: Together they plotted to deliver poison hidden in pastries.

sentences.zh: 六月，壬午，中宗崩於神龍殿。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on renwu, Emperor Zhongzong died in the Hall of Divine Dragon.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on renwu, Emperor Zhongzong collapsed and died in the Hall of Divine Dragon.

sentences.zh: 韋後秘不發喪，自總庶政。

translations.literal: Empress Wei secretly withheld announcement of the death and herself took charge of all government.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wei concealed the emperor's death and assumed control of the government.

sentences.zh: 癸未，召諸宰相入禁中，征諸府兵五萬人屯京城，使駙馬都尉韋捷、韋灌、衞尉卿韋璿、左千牛中郎將韋璿、長安令韋播、郎將髙嵩等分領之。

translations.literal: On guiwei, she summoned all chancellors into the forbidden precincts, requisitioned fifty thousand militia from the various prefectures to garrison the capital, and had Commandant-in-Chief of Horse Wei Jie, Wei Guan, Chamberlain Wei Xuan, Left Chief of the Thousand-Ox Mid-Ranking General Wei Xuan, Magistrate of Chang'an Wei Bo, and General Gao Song and others divide command among them.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei she called the chancellors into the inner palace, mobilized fifty thousand militiamen from outlying prefectures to occupy the capital, and divided command among her kin: Commandants-in-Chief of Horse Wei Jie and Wei Guan, Chamberlain Wei Xuan, Left Chief of the Thousand-Ox Mid-Ranking General Wei Xuan, Chang'an Magistrate Wei Bo, General Gao Song, and others.

sentences.zh: 璿，温之族弟；

translations.literal: Xuan was Clan-younger-brother of Wen;
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was a younger clansman of Wen.

sentences.zh: 播，從子；

translations.literal: Bo was a nephew's son;
translations.idiomatic: Bo was Wen's grand-nephew.

sentences.zh: 嵩；

translations.literal: Song;
translations.idiomatic: Song—

sentences.zh: 其甥也。

translations.literal: was his sister's son.
translations.idiomatic: was his nephew.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人韋元徼巡六街。

translations.literal: Secretariat Drafter Wei Yuanjiao patrolled the Six Avenues.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Drafter Wei Yuanjiao was sent to patrol the Six Avenues.

sentences.zh: 又命左監門大將軍兼内侍薛思簡等，將兵五百人馳驛戍均州，以備譙王重福。

translations.literal: She further ordered Left Grand General of the Gate Guards and concurrent Inner Attendant Xue Sijian and others to lead five hundred troops post-haste by relay to garrison Junzhou, to guard against Prince of Qiao Chongfu.
translations.idiomatic: She also ordered Xue Sijian, Left Grand General of the Gate Guards who doubled as Inner Attendant, to rush five hundred men by post-horse to garrison Junzhou against Prince of Qiao Chongfu.

sentences.zh: 以刑部尚書裴談、工部尚書張錫並同中書門下三品，仍充東都留守。

translations.literal: Minister of Justice Pei Tan and Minister of Works Zhang Xi were both made Fellows of the Third Rank of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and still served as Eastern Capital regents.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Tan, Minister of Justice, and Zhang Xi, Minister of Works, were both promoted to Fellows of the Third Rank and left in place as Eastern Capital regents.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書張嘉福、中書侍郎岑羲、吏部侍郎崔湜並同平章事。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Zhang Jiafu, Secretariat Vice Minister Cen Xi, and Vice Minister of Personnel Cui Shi were all made Equally Participating in Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiafu, Minister of Personnel; Cen Xi, Secretariat Vice Minister; and Cui Shi, Vice Minister of Personnel—all were appointed Equally Participating in Affairs.

sentences.zh: 羲，長倩之子也。

translations.literal: Xi was the son of Changqian.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was the son of Cen Changqian.

sentences.zh: 太平公主與上官昭容謀草遺制，立温王重茂爲皇太子，皇后知政事，相王旦參謀政事。

translations.literal: Princess Taiping and Shangguan Zhaorong plotted to draft the deathbed decree, installing Prince of Wen Chongmao as crown prince, the empress to manage state affairs, and Prince of Xiang Dan to assist in deliberating over state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Taiping and the Lady of Bright Attainment Shangguan plotted a deathbed decree naming Prince Wen Chongmao crown prince, putting the empress in charge of government while Prince of Xiang Dan would counsel on affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 宗楚客密謂韋温曰：「相王輔政，於理非宜；

translations.literal: Zong Chuke secretly said to Wei Wen: "The Prince of Xiang assisting in government is not proper in principle;
translations.idiomatic: Zong Chuke whispered to Wei Wen: "For the Prince of Xiang to share power makes no sense;

sentences.zh: 且於皇后，嫂叔不通問，聽朝之際，何以爲禮？」

translations.literal: moreover, between empress and him—sister-in-law and younger brother-in-law do not exchange inquiries; at the time of hearing court, what rites would apply?"
translations.idiomatic: besides, as empress and brother-in-law they may not even greet each other—how could they share an audience without scandal?"

sentences.zh: 遂帥諸宰相表請皇后臨朝，罷相王政事。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led all chancellors in a memorial requesting the empress to preside over court and removing the Prince of Xiang from participation in government.
translations.idiomatic: He then rallied the chancellors to petition for the empress to rule from the throne and strip the Prince of Xiang of his political role.

sentences.zh: 蘇瑰曰：「遺詔豈可改邪！」

translations.literal: Su Gui said: "How can the deathbed decree be altered!"
translations.idiomatic: Su Gui protested: "You cannot rewrite a deathbed decree!"

sentences.zh: 温、楚客怒，瑰懼而從之，乃以相王爲太子太師。

translations.literal: Wen and Chuke were angry; Gui feared and yielded, and so the Prince of Xiang was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Wen and Zong Chuke flew into a rage; frightened, Su Gui backed down, and Prince of Xiang was relegated to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 甲申，梓宮遷御太極殿，集百官，發喪，皇后臨朝攝政，赦天下，改元唐隆。

translations.literal: On jiashen, the imperial coffin was moved to the Hall of Supreme Ultimate; the hundred officials were assembled, mourning was proclaimed, the empress presided over court as regent, amnesty was granted to All-under-Heaven, and the era name was changed to Tanglong.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen the coffin was brought to the Hall of Supreme Ultimate. Officials assembled, mourning was declared, and the empress took the throne as regent. She declared a general amnesty and changed the era name to Tanglong.

sentences.zh: 進相王旦爲太尉，雍王守禮爲幽王，壽春王成器爲宋王，以從人望。

translations.literal: Prince of Xiang Dan was advanced to Grand Commandant, Prince of Yong Shouli to Prince of You, Prince of Shouchun Chengqi to Prince of Song, to follow popular expectation.
translations.idiomatic: To satisfy public sentiment she elevated Prince of Xiang Dan to Grand Commandant, Prince of Yong Shouli to Prince of You, and Prince of Shouchun Chengqi to Prince of Song.

sentences.zh: 命韋温總知内外守捉兵馬事。

translations.literal: She ordered Wei Wen to oversee in full the inner and outer guard and garrison troops and horses affairs.
translations.idiomatic: She put Wei Wen in overall command of palace and capital military forces.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，殤帝即位，時年十六。

translations.literal: On dinghai, the Shang Emperor ascended the throne; he was then sixteen years old.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai the young emperor Li Chongmao took the throne at sixteen.

sentences.zh: 尊皇后爲皇太后；

translations.literal: The empress was honored as empress dowager;
translations.idiomatic: The empress was elevated to empress dowager;

sentences.zh: 立妃陸氏爲皇后。

translations.literal: Consort Lu was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Lu was crowned empress.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，命紀處訥持節巡撫關内道，岑羲河南道，張嘉福河北道。

translations.literal: On renchen, Ji Chuna was ordered to hold credentials and tour and pacify the Guannei Circuit, Cen Xi the Henan Circuit, and Zhang Jiafu the Hebei Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen Ji Chuna was dispatched with imperial credentials to inspect the Guannei Circuit, Cen Xi the Henan Circuit, and Zhang Jiafu the Hebei Circuit.

sentences.zh: 宗楚客與太常卿武延秀、司農卿趙履温、國子祭酒葉靜能及諸韋共勸韋後遵武後故事，南北衞軍、台閣要司皆以韋氏子弟領之，廣聚黨衆，中外連結。

translations.literal: Zong Chuke, together with Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Wu Yanxiu, Director of the Court of the Imperial Granary Zhao Lüwen, Director of the Directorate of Education Ye Jingneng, and the various Weis jointly urged Empress Wei to follow Empress Wu's precedent: the southern and northern guard armies and key posts in the ministries and halls were all led by Wei clan youths and younger brothers; they broadly gathered faction followers and linked inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Chuke, Wu Yanxiu, Zhao Lüwen, Ye Jingneng, and the Wei kin urged Empress Wei to replay Empress Wu's coup—placing Wei clansmen in the palace guards and every vital post, building a web of allies from court to capital.

sentences.zh: 楚客又密上書稱引圖讖，謂韋氏宜革唐命。

translations.literal: Chuke further secretly submitted a memorial citing prophecies and charts, saying the Wei clan ought to change the Tang mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Chuke also sent a secret memorial citing prophetic texts, arguing that Heaven intended the Wei clan to seize the Tang throne.

sentences.zh: 謀害殤帝，深忌相王及太平公主，密與韋温、安樂公主謀去之。

translations.literal: They plotted to harm the Shang Emperor, deeply resented the Prince of Xiang and Princess Taiping, and secretly with Wei Wen and Princess Anle plotted to remove them.
translations.idiomatic: They conspired to kill the young emperor, eyed the Prince of Xiang and Princess Taiping with deep suspicion, and secretly joined Wei Wen and Princess Anle in plotting their elimination.

sentences.zh: 相王子臨淄王隆基，先罷潞州別駕，在京師，陰聚才勇之士，謀匡復社稷。

translations.literal: Prince of Xiang's son Prince of Linzi Longji, having earlier been removed as Vice Prefect of Luzhou, was in the capital, secretly gathering men of talent and courage, plotting to restore the altar and land.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xiang's son, Prince of Linzi Li Longji, had lately left his post as Vice Prefect of Luzhou and was in the capital secretly recruiting bold and capable men, planning to rescue the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗選官戸及蕃口驍勇者，著虎文衣，跨豹文韉，從遊獵，於馬前射禽獸，謂之百騎；

translations.literal: Initially, Taizong selected registered households and frontier tribesmen who were fierce and brave, dressed them in tiger-pattern robes, mounted leopard-pattern saddles, and had them follow on hunts, shooting birds and beasts before his horse—they were called the Hundred Riders;
translations.idiomatic: In the beginning Taizong had chosen fierce fighters from registered households and tribal recruits, clothed them in tiger-striped garb and leopard-skinned saddles, and kept them at his side on hunts to shoot game from horseback—a corps known as the Hundred Riders;

sentences.zh: 則天時稍增爲千騎，隸左右羽林；

translations.literal: In Empress Wu's time they were gradually increased to the Thousand Riders, subordinate to the Left and Right Palace Guards;
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu the corps grew to the Thousand Riders and was attached to the Left and Right Forest Army;

sentences.zh: 中宗謂之萬騎，置使以領之。

translations.literal: Zhongzong called them the Ten Thousand Riders and established commissioners to command them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong expanded them into the Ten Thousand Riders and appointed overseers to lead them.

sentences.zh: 隆基皆厚結其豪傑。

translations.literal: Longji all thickly bonded with their champions.
translations.idiomatic: Longji won over their leading men with generous patronage.

sentences.zh: 兵部侍郎崔日用素附韋、武，與宗楚客善，知楚客謀，恐禍及己，遣寶昌寺僧普潤密詣隆基告之，勸其速發。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of War Cui Riyong had long attached himself to the Wei and Wu factions, was on good terms with Zong Chuke, learned of Chuke's plot, feared disaster would reach himself, and sent the monk Purun of Baochang Temple secretly to Longji to inform him, urging him to act quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Riyong, Vice Minister of War, had long courted the Wei and Wu factions and was close to Zong Chuke. When he learned of the plot he feared he would be swept up in the purge and sent the monk Purun of Baochang Temple to warn Longji in secret, urging him to strike at once.

sentences.zh: 隆基乃與太平公主及公主子衞尉卿薛崇暕、苑總監贛人鐘紹京、尚衣奏御王崇曄、前朝邑尉劉幽求、利仁府折衝麻嗣宗謀先事誅之。

translations.literal: Longji then with Princess Taiping and the princess's son Chamberlain Xue Chongjian, Director of the Imperial Park Zhong Shaojing of Gan, Master of Imperial Vestments Wang Chongye, former Magistrate of Chaoyi Liu Youqiu, and Colonel of Liren Prefecture Ma Sizong plotted to strike first and execute them.
translations.idiomatic: Longji then joined Princess Taiping, her son Xue Chongjian of the Chamberlain's court, park director Zhong Shaojing, imperial wardrobe officer Wang Chongye, former Chaoyi magistrate Liu Youqiu, and Liren Colonel Ma Sizong in a plan to kill the conspirators before they could act.

sentences.zh: 韋播、髙嵩數榜捶萬騎，欲以立威，萬騎皆怨。

translations.literal: Wei Bo and Gao Song repeatedly had the Ten Thousand Riders beaten with clubs to establish authority; the Ten Thousand Riders all resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Bo and Gao Song repeatedly flogged the Ten Thousand Riders to assert their authority, earning the corps's bitter hatred.

sentences.zh: 果毅葛福順、陳玄禮見隆基訴之，隆基諷以誅諸韋，皆踴躍請以死自效。

translations.literal: Corps officers Ge Fushun and Chen Xuanli came to Longji to complain; Longji intimated that the various Weis should be executed, and all eagerly requested to devote their lives in service.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Fushun and Chen Xuanli, officers of the corps, came to Longji with their grievances. He hinted at a strike against the Wei clan, and they eagerly volunteered their lives for the cause.

sentences.zh: 萬騎果毅李仙鳧亦預其謀。

translations.literal: Ten Thousand Riders corps officer Li Xianfu also participated in the plot.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xianfu, another corps officer of the Ten Thousand Riders, was in on the conspiracy as well.

sentences.zh: 或謂隆基當啓相王，隆基曰：「我曹爲此以徇社稷，事成福歸於王，不成以身死之，不以累王也。

translations.literal: Someone said Longji ought to inform the Prince of Xiang; Longji said: "We do this to give our bodies for the altar and land; if it succeeds, the blessing returns to the prince; if not, we die by our own bodies and do not involve the prince.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Longji to tell the Prince of Xiang first. He refused: "We undertake this for the realm alone. If we succeed, the credit belongs to my father; if we fail, we die ourselves and will not drag him down.

sentences.zh: 今啓而見從，則王預危事；

translations.literal: If now we inform him and he consents, then the prince enters a dangerous affair;
translations.idiomatic: If I tell him and he agrees, he becomes an accomplice in a perilous plot;

sentences.zh: 不從，將敗大計。」

translations.literal: if he does not consent, the great plan will be ruined."
translations.idiomatic: if he refuses, the whole enterprise collapses."

sentences.zh: 遂不啓。

translations.literal: Thereupon he did not inform him.
translations.idiomatic: And so he kept silent.

sentences.zh: 庚子，晡時，隆基微服與幽求等入苑中，會鐘紹京廨捨；

translations.literal: On gengzi, at the hour of shen (late afternoon), Longji in plain dress with Youqiu and others entered the park and met at Zhong Shaojing's official residence;
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, in late afternoon, Longji slipped in disguised with Liu Youqiu and the others and rendezvoused at Zhong Shaojing's office in the imperial park.

sentences.zh: 紹京悔，欲拒之，其妻許氏曰：「忘身徇國，神必助之。

translations.literal: Shaojing repented and wished to refuse them; his wife Lady Xu said: "Forgetting one's body to serve the state—spirits will surely aid this.
translations.idiomatic: Shaojing wavered and tried to turn them away, but his wife Lady Xu said: "Sacrifice yourself for the dynasty and Heaven itself will lend a hand.

sentences.zh: 且同謀素定，今雖不行，庸得免乎！」

translations.literal: Moreover the joint plot was long settled; even if you do not act now, how could you escape!"
translations.idiomatic: You were party to this from the start—if you hang back now, do you truly think you can walk away?"

sentences.zh: 紹京乃趨出拜謁，隆基執其手與坐。

translations.literal: Shaojing then hurried out to pay respects; Longji took his hand and sat with him.
translations.idiomatic: Shaojing rushed out to salute them; Longji took his hand and seated him beside him.

sentences.zh: 時羽林將士皆屯玄武門，逮夜，葛福順、李仙鳧皆至隆基所，請號而行。

translations.literal: At that time the Forest Army officers and soldiers all garrisoned at the Dark Warrior Gate; when night came, Ge Fushun and Li Xianfu all arrived at Longji's place and requested the signal to march.
translations.idiomatic: The Forest Army had massed at the Dark Warrior Gate. By nightfall Ge Fushun and Li Xianfu had joined Longji and asked for the word to move.

sentences.zh: 向二鼓，天星散落如雪，劉幽求曰：「天意如此，時不可失！」

translations.literal: Approaching the second watch, stars in the sky scattered like snow; Liu Youqiu said: "Heaven's intent is thus—the time must not be lost!"
translations.idiomatic: Around the second watch the sky burst into a shower of falling stars. Liu Youqiu cried: "Heaven itself signals us—we must not hesitate!"

sentences.zh: 福順拔劍直入羽林營，斬韋璿、韋播、髙嵩以徇，曰：「韋後鴆殺先帝，謀危社稷。

translations.literal: Fushun drew his sword and went straight into the Forest Army camp, beheaded Wei Xuan, Wei Bo, and Gao Song as a public warning, and said: "Empress Wei poisoned the late emperor and plotted to endanger the altar and land.
translations.idiomatic: Fushun drew his sword, marched straight into the Forest Army camp, and executed Wei Xuan, Wei Bo, and Gao Song as an example, proclaiming: "Empress Wei murdered the late emperor and plotted to topple the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 今夕當共誅諸韋，馬鞭以上皆斬之！

translations.literal: Tonight we together shall execute the various Weis—all from horsewhip rank upward shall be beheaded!
translations.idiomatic: Tonight we purge every Wei from horsewhip rank on up!

sentences.zh: 立相王以安天下。

translations.literal: Establish the Prince of Xiang to settle All-under-Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Install the Prince of Xiang to restore order to the realm.

sentences.zh: 敢有懷兩端助逆黨者，罪及三族！」

translations.literal: Whoever dares to harbor two minds and aid the rebellious faction—punishment extends to three clans!"
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who wavers or aids the traitors will face execution for three generations of kin!"

sentences.zh: 羽林之士皆欣然聽命。

translations.literal: The Forest Army warriors all gladly obeyed orders.
translations.idiomatic: The Forest Army men accepted their orders with enthusiasm.

sentences.zh: 乃送璿等首於隆基，隆基取火視之，遂與幽求等出苑南門，紹京帥丁匠二百餘人，執斧鋸以從。

translations.literal: They then sent the heads of Xuan and the others to Longji; Longji took fire to examine them, then with Youqiu and others went out the park's south gate; Shaojing led more than two hundred laborers, carrying axes and saws to follow.
translations.idiomatic: The heads were delivered to Longji, who held a torch to inspect them, then marched out the park's south gate with Youqiu and the rest. Shaojing followed with over two hundred craftsmen bearing axes and saws.

sentences.zh: 使福順將左萬騎攻玄德門，仙鳧將右萬騎攻白獸門，約會於凌煙閣前，即大噪，福順等殺守門將，斬關而入。

translations.literal: He sent Fushun to lead the Left Ten Thousand Riders to attack the Xuan virtue Gate, Xianfu the Right Ten Thousand Riders to attack the White Beast Gate; they were to meet before the Hall of Splendid Portraits, then raise a great clamor; Fushun and the others killed the gate-keeping generals, cut the barrier and entered.
translations.idiomatic: Fushun was sent with the Left Ten Thousand Riders against the Gate of Hidden Virtue, Xianfu with the Right against the Gate of the White Beast. They were to rally at the Hall of Splendid Portraits, raise a great shout, and break through—Fushun's men killed the gate commanders and forced their way in.

sentences.zh: 隆基勒兵玄武門外，三鼓，聞聲，帥總監及羽林兵而入，諸衞兵在太極殿宿衞梓宮者，聞噪聲，皆被甲應之。

translations.literal: Longji restrained troops outside the Dark Warrior Gate; at the third watch, hearing the noise, he led the director and Forest Army troops inward; the various guard soldiers garrisoning the imperial coffin at the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, hearing the clamor, all donned armor and responded.
translations.idiomatic: Longji held his force at the Dark Warrior Gate. At the third watch, hearing the uproar, he entered with Zhong Shaojing and the Forest Army. Palace guards stationed at the Hall of Supreme Ultimate to watch over the coffin heard the commotion, armored themselves, and joined in.

sentences.zh: 韋後惶惑走入飛騎營，有飛騎斬首獻於隆基。

translations.literal: Empress Wei in panic and confusion ran into the Flying Cavalry camp; a Flying Cavalry man beheaded her and presented the head to Longji.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wei fled in panic toward the Flying Cavalry camp, where one of the riders cut off her head and presented it to Longji.

sentences.zh: 安樂公主方照鏡畫眉，軍士斬之。

translations.literal: Princess Anle was just then looking in the mirror drawing her eyebrows; soldiers beheaded her.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Anle was applying makeup before her mirror when soldiers killed her.

sentences.zh: 斬武延秀於肅章門外，斬内將軍賀婁氏於太極殿西。

translations.literal: Wu Yanxiu was beheaded outside the Gate of Majestic Seal; Inner General Helou shi was beheaded west of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yanxiu was executed outside the Gate of Majestic Seal; Inner General Lady Helou was slain west of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 初，上官昭容引其從母之子王昱爲左拾遺，昱説昭容母鄭氏曰：「武氏，天之所廢，不可興也。

translations.literal: Initially, Shangguan Zhaorong brought in her mother's sister's son Wang Yu as Left Remonstrance Aide; Yu persuaded Zhaorong's mother Lady Zheng, saying: "The Wu clan—Heaven has discarded them; they cannot be revived.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Shangguan Zhaorong had installed her cousin Wang Yu as Left Remonstrance Aide. Wang Yu warned Lady Zheng, the Lady of Bright Attainment's mother: "Heaven itself rejected the Wu clan—it must not rise again.

sentences.zh: 今婕妤附於三思，此滅族之道也，願姨思之！」

translations.literal: Now the Lady of Handsome Fairness attaches to Sansi—this is the path to extermination of the clan; I wish Aunt would consider it!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet your daughter has tied herself to Sansi—that is the road to annihilation for the whole family. Please think on this, Aunt!"

sentences.zh: 鄭氏以戒昭容，昭容弗聽。

translations.literal: Lady Zheng used this to warn Zhaorong; Zhaorong would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zheng passed the warning to her daughter, but Shangguan would not heed it.

sentences.zh: 及太子重俊起兵誅三思，索昭容，昭容始懼，思昱言；

translations.literal: When the crown prince Chongjun raised troops to execute Sansi and sought Zhaorong, Zhaorong first grew afraid and recalled Yu's words;
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Chongjun took up arms against Sansi and came hunting for Shangguan, she at last grew afraid and remembered Wang Yu's warning;

sentences.zh: 自是心附帝室，與安樂公主各樹朋黨。

translations.literal: from then her heart attached to the imperial house, and she and Princess Anle each raised their own faction cliques.
translations.idiomatic: thereafter she shifted her loyalty toward the throne and fell into rivalry with Princess Anle, each building a separate faction.

sentences.zh: 及中宗崩，昭容草遺制立温王，以相王輔政；

translations.literal: When Zhongzong died, Zhaorong drafted the deathbed decree installing Prince of Wen, with the Prince of Xiang assisting in government;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong died, Shangguan drafted a deathbed decree naming Prince Wen heir and the Prince of Xiang as regent;

sentences.zh: 宗、韋改之。

translations.literal: Zong and Wei altered it.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Chuke and the Wei faction rewrote it.

sentences.zh: 及隆基入宮，昭容執燭帥宮入迎之，以制草示劉幽求。

translations.literal: When Longji entered the palace, Zhaorong held a candle and led palace women to welcome him, showing the draft decree to Liu Youqiu.
translations.idiomatic: When Longji entered the palace, Shangguan came forward with a candle, leading palace women to greet him, and showed Liu Youqiu the draft decree.

sentences.zh: 幽求爲之言，隆基不許，斬於旗下。

translations.literal: Youqiu spoke on her behalf; Longji did not assent and beheaded her beneath the banner.
translations.idiomatic: Youqiu pleaded for her, but Longji refused and had her executed on the spot beneath his banner.

sentences.zh: 時少帝在太極殿，劉幽求曰：「衆約今夕共立相王，何不早定！」

translations.literal: At that time the Lesser Emperor was in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate; Liu Youqiu said: "The crowd agreed tonight jointly to establish the Prince of Xiang—why not settle it early!"
translations.idiomatic: The young emperor still sat in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate when Liu Youqiu said: "We all pledged tonight to raise the Prince of Xiang—why delay any longer?"

sentences.zh: 隆基遽止之，捕索諸韋在宮中及守諸門，並素爲韋後所親信者皆斬之。

translations.literal: Longji hastily stopped him, searched out and seized all Weis in the palace and guarding the various gates, and all who had long been trusted intimates of Empress Wei—all were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Longji cut him off and ordered a hunt through the palace: every Wei still inside, every gate still held by Empress Wei's favorites—all were put to the sword.

sentences.zh: 比曉，内外皆定。

translations.literal: By dawn, inside and outside were all settled.
translations.idiomatic: By daybreak the palace and capital were secure.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，隆基出見相王，叩頭謝不先啓之罪。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Longji went out to see the Prince of Xiang, knocked his head and apologized for the crime of not informing him first.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi Longji went to his father and kowtowed, begging forgiveness for having acted without telling him first.

sentences.zh: 相王抱之泣曰：「社稷宗廟不墜於地，汝之力也！」

translations.literal: The Prince of Xiang embraced him weeping and said: "The altar of state and the ancestral temple did not fall to earth—this is your power!"
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xiang held him and wept: "You alone kept the dynasty from collapse!"

sentences.zh: 遂迎相王入輔少帝。

translations.literal: Thereupon he welcomed the Prince of Xiang in to assist the Lesser Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He then brought the Prince of Xiang in to guide the young emperor.

sentences.zh: 閉宮門及京城門，分遣萬騎收捕諸韋親黨。

translations.literal: Palace gates and capital gates were closed; the Ten Thousand Riders were sent separately to capture the various Wei kin and faction members.
translations.idiomatic: The palace and city gates were sealed shut while the Ten Thousand Riders fanned out to hunt down the Wei clan and their allies.

sentences.zh: 斬太子少保、同中書門下三品韋温於東市之北。

translations.literal: Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Fellow of the Third Rank Wei Wen was beheaded north of the Eastern Market.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Wen, Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Fellow of the Third Rank, was executed north of the Eastern Market.

sentences.zh: 中書令宗楚客衣斬衰、乘靑驢逃出，至通化門，門者曰：「公，宗尚書也。」

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Zong Chuke, dressed in cut hemp mourning, rode a gray donkey to flee; reaching the Tonghua Gate, the gatekeeper said: "Sir, you are Minister Zong."
translations.idiomatic: Zong Chuke, Grand Counselor of the Secretariat, fled in coarse mourning robes on a gray donkey. At the Tonghua Gate the guard called out: "You're Minister Zong."

sentences.zh: 去布帽，執而斬之，並斬其弟晉卿。

translations.literal: He removed his cloth cap; they seized and beheaded him, and also beheaded his younger brother Jinqing.
translations.idiomatic: They tore off his cloth cap, seized him, and cut off his head—along with his brother Jinqing's.

sentences.zh: 相王奉少帝御安福門，慰諭百姓。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xiang attended the Lesser Emperor at the Gate of Settled Blessings and comforted and instructed the common people.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xiang led the young emperor to the Gate of Settled Blessings to reassure the populace.

sentences.zh: 初，趙履温傾國資以奉安樂公主，爲之起第捨，築台穿池無休已，擫紫衫，以項挽公主犢車。

translations.literal: Initially, Zhao Lüwen exhausted the state's resources to serve Princess Anle, built mansions for her, raised platforms and dug ponds without cease, clutched his purple robe, and with his neck pulled the princess's ox cart.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Lüwen had squandered the treasury on Princess Anle, building her ever grander estates with terraces and ponds without end—even grabbing his own purple official robe to use his neck as a trace for her ox-drawn carriage.

sentences.zh: 公主死，履温馳詣安福樓下舞蹈稱萬歳；

translations.literal: When the princess died, Lüwen galloped to below the Tower of Settled Blessings and danced, calling "Ten thousand years!";
translations.idiomatic: When the princess fell, Lüwen raced to the Tower of Settled Blessings and danced there shouting "Long live the emperor!"

sentences.zh: 聲未絶，相王命萬騎斬之。

translations.literal: Before the voice had ceased, the Prince of Xiang ordered the Ten Thousand Riders to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Before the shout had faded, the Prince of Xiang ordered the Ten Thousand Riders to cut him down.

sentences.zh: 百姓怨其勞役，爭割其肉，立盡。

translations.literal: The common people resented his corvée labor; they vied to slice his flesh, and it was gone in an instant.
translations.idiomatic: The people, furious at the forced labor he had imposed, tore his flesh apart on the spot until nothing remained.

sentences.zh: 秘書監汴王邕娶韋後妹崇國夫人，與御史大夫竇從一各手斬其妻首以獻。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Prince of Bian Yong had married Empress Wei's younger sister Lady of Chongguo; he and Censor-in-Chief Dou Congyi each with their own hands beheaded their wives' heads and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Bian Yong, Director of the Secretariat, had married Empress Wei's sister, the Lady of Chongguo; he and Censor-in-Chief Dou Congyi each personally beheaded his own wife and presented the heads.

sentences.zh: 邕，鳳之孫也。

translations.literal: Yong was the grandson of Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was a grandson of Dou Feng.

sentences.zh: 左僕射、，同中書門下三品韋巨源聞亂，家人勸之逃匿，巨源曰：「吾位大臣，豈可聞難不赴！」

translations.literal: Left Vice Director, , Fellow of the Third Rank Wei Juyuan heard of the disorder; his family urged him to flee and hide; Juyuan said: "I hold the rank of great minister—how could I hear of difficulty and not go!"
translations.idiomatic: Wei Juyuan, Left Vice Director and Fellow of the Third Rank, heard of the uprising. His family begged him to hide, but he said: "I am a chief minister—how can I flee when the realm is in crisis?"

sentences.zh: 出至都街，爲亂兵所殺，時年八十。

translations.literal: He went out to the capital avenue and was killed by disorderly troops; he was then eighty years old.
translations.idiomatic: He walked out into the main avenue and was cut down by the mutineers. He was eighty.

sentences.zh: 於是梟馬秦客、楊均、葉靜能等首，屍韋後於市。

translations.literal: Thereupon the heads of Ma Qinke, Yang Jun, Ye Jingneng and others were displayed; Empress Wei's corpse was exposed in the market.
translations.idiomatic: The heads of Ma Qinke, Yang Jun, Ye Jingneng, and others were put on public display, and Empress Wei's body was paraded through the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 崔日用將兵誅諸韋於杜曲，襁褓兒無免者，諸杜濫死非一。

translations.literal: Cui Riyong led troops to execute the various Weis at Duqu; infants in swaddling clothes had none spared; among the various Dus wrongly killed there were not a few.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Riyong marched on Duqu to slaughter the Wei clan there; not even infants were spared, and many unrelated people surnamed Du died in the bloodletting.

sentences.zh: 是日，赦天下，云：「逆賊魁首已誅，自餘支黨一無所問。」

translations.literal: That day, amnesty was granted to All-under-Heaven, stating: "The rebel chiefs' ringleaders have been executed; as for the remaining branch factions, nothing is to be inquired into."
translations.idiomatic: That day a general amnesty was proclaimed: "The rebel leaders have been cut down; all lesser followers are absolved."

sentences.zh: 以臨淄王隆基爲平王，兼知内外閒廄，押左右廂萬騎。

translations.literal: Prince of Linzi Longji was made Prince of Ping, concurrently managing inner and outer stables and pastures, and commanding the Left and Right Flank Ten Thousand Riders.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Linzi Li Longji was ennobled as Prince of Ping, put in charge of the imperial stables, and given command of the Left and Right Ten Thousand Riders.

sentences.zh: 薛崇暕賜爵立節王。

translations.literal: Xue Chongxian was granted the title Prince Who Establishes Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Chongxian was ennobled as Prince Who Establishes Integrity.

sentences.zh: 以鐘紹京守中書侍郎，劉幽求守中書舍人，並參知機務。

translations.literal: Zhong Shaojing was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, Liu Youqiu Vice Director of the Secretariat Chancellery, both participating in handling state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Shaojing was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Liu Youqiu Vice Chancellor, both joining in the daily management of government.

sentences.zh: 麻嗣宗行左金吾衞中郎將。

translations.literal: Ma Sizong acted as Captain in the Left Golden Guard Legion.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sizong served as captain in the Left Golden Guard.

sentences.zh: 武氏宗屬，誅死流竄殆盡。

translations.literal: Wu clan kinsmen were put to death and exiled, nearly to the last.
translations.idiomatic: Members of the Wu clan were executed or banished until almost none remained.

sentences.zh: 侍中紀處訥行至華州，吏部尚書、同平章事張嘉福行至懷州，皆收斬之。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary Ji Chuna, traveling, reached Hua Prefecture; Minister of Personnel and Chief Minister Zhang Jiafu, traveling, reached Huai Prefecture—both were seized and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Chuna, Attendant-in-Ordinary, was caught at Hua Prefecture while fleeing; Zhang Jiafu, Minister of Personnel and Chief Minister, was caught at Huai Prefecture—both were executed.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，劉幽求在太極殿，有宮人與宦官令幽求作制書立太后，幽求曰：「國有大難，人情不安，山陵未畢，遽立太后，不可。」

translations.literal: On renyin, Liu Youqiu was in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate. Palace women and eunuchs ordered Youqiu to draft an edict installing an empress dowager. Youqiu said: "The state faces great calamity; people's hearts are unsettled; the imperial tomb rites are not yet complete—to hastily install an empress dowager cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: On renyin Liu Youqiu was in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate when palace women and eunuchs pressed him to draft an edict elevating an empress dowager. He refused: "The realm is in crisis, the people are uneasy, and the late emperor's funeral is unfinished—to rush a regency now would be wrong."

sentences.zh: 平王隆基曰：「此勿輕言。」

translations.literal: Prince of Ping Longji said: "Do not speak lightly of this."
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Ping Longji warned: "Do not bandy such talk."

sentences.zh: 遣十道使繼璽書宣撫，及詣均州宣慰譙王重福。

translations.literal: Ten circuit commissioners were dispatched bearing successive imperial seals to proclaim reassurance; some also went to Jun Prefecture to console Prince of Qiao Zhongfu.
translations.idiomatic: Ten circuit commissioners were sent out with successive imperial edicts to calm the provinces, and envoys were also dispatched to Jun Prefecture to reassure Prince of Qiao Zhongfu.

sentences.zh: 貶竇從一爲濠州司馬。

translations.literal: Dou Congyi was demoted to Military Adjutant of Hao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Congyi was demoted to adjutant of Hao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 罷諸公主府官。

translations.literal: The officials of all princesses' households were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: All offices attached to princess households were abolished.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，太平公主傳少帝命，請讓位於相王，相王固辭。

translations.literal: On guimao, Princess Taiping relayed the Lesser Emperor's order, asking to yield the throne to the Prince of Xiang; the Prince of Xiang firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao Princess Taiping announced on the young emperor's behalf that he wished to abdicate in favor of the Prince of Xiang, who steadfastly refused.

sentences.zh: 以平王隆基爲殿中監、同中書門下三品，以宋王成器爲左衞大將軍，衡陽王成義爲右衞大將軍，巴陵王隆范爲左羽林大將軍，彭城王隆業爲右羽林大將軍，光祿少卿嗣道王微檢校右金吾衞大將軍。

translations.literal: Prince of Ping Longji was made Director of the Palace Administration and Fellow of the Third Rank; Prince of Song Chengqi was made General of the Left Guard; Prince of Hengyang Chengyi General of the Right Guard; Prince of Baling Longfan General of the Left Forest Guard; Prince of Pengcheng Longye General of the Right Forest Guard; Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Prince of Sidao Wei was made acting General of the Right Golden Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Ping Longji was appointed Director of the Palace Administration and Fellow of the Third Rank; Prince of Song Chengqi became General of the Left Guard; Prince of Hengyang Chengyi, General of the Right Guard; Prince of Baling Longfan, General of the Left Forest Guard; Prince of Pengcheng Longye, General of the Right Forest Guard; and Prince of Sidao Wei, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, acting General of the Right Golden Guard.

sentences.zh: 微，元慶之孫也。

translations.literal: Wei was the grandson of Yuanqing.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was a grandson of Yuanqing.

sentences.zh: 以黃門侍郎李日知、中書侍郎鐘紹京並同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat Li Rizhi and Vice Director of the Secretariat Zhong Shaojing were both made Fellows of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: Li Rizhi, Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Zhong Shaojing, Vice Director of the Secretariat, were both elevated to Fellows of the Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 太平公主之子薛崇訓爲右千牛衞將軍。

translations.literal: Princess Taiping's son Xue Chongxun was made General of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Taiping's son Xue Chongxun was appointed General of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard.

sentences.zh: 隆基有二奴：王毛仲、李守德，皆趫勇善騎射，常侍衞左右。

translations.literal: Longji had two slaves: Wang Maochong and Li Shoude, both nimble and brave, skilled at mounted archery, constantly attending at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Longji kept two bondsmen, Wang Maochong and Li Shoude—both fleet, fierce, and expert horsemen—who were always at his side.

sentences.zh: 隆基之入苑中也，毛仲避匿不從，事定數日方歸，隆基不之責，仍超拜將軍。

translations.literal: When Longji entered the park, Maochong hid and did not follow; several days after affairs were settled he returned; Longji did not blame him and even promoted him to general.
translations.idiomatic: When Longji marched into the park, Maochong went into hiding and did not join him; only days after the coup did he reappear. Longji did not reproach him and even promoted him to general.

sentences.zh: 毛仲，本髙麗也。

translations.literal: Maochong was originally from Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Maochong was a native of Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 汴王邕貶沁州刺史，左散騎常侍、駙馬都尉楊愼交貶巴州刺史，中書令蕭至忠貶許州刺史，兵部尚書、同中書門下三品韋嗣立貶宋州刺史，中書侍郎、同平章事趙彦昭貶絳州刺史，吏部侍郎、同平章事崔湜貶華州刺史。

translations.literal: Prince of Bian Yong was demoted to Prefect of Qin Prefecture; Left Regular Attendant and Commandant of Cavalry Yang Shenjiao to Prefect of Ba Prefecture; Secretariat Director Xiao Zhizhong to Prefect of Xu Prefecture; Minister of War and Fellow of the Third Rank Wei Sili to Prefect of Song Prefecture; Vice Director of the Secretariat and Chief Minister Zhao Yanzhao to Prefect of Jiang Prefecture; Vice Minister of Personnel and Chief Minister Cui Shi to Prefect of Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Bian Yong was demoted to prefect of Qin; Yang Shenjiao, Left Regular Attendant and Commandant of Cavalry, to prefect of Ba; Xiao Zhizhong, Secretariat Director, to prefect of Xu; Wei Sili, Minister of War and Fellow of the Third Rank, to prefect of Song; Zhao Yanzhao, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Chief Minister, to prefect of Jiang; and Cui Shi, Vice Minister of Personnel and Chief Minister, to prefect of Hua.

sentences.zh: 劉幽求言於宋王成器、平王隆基曰：「相王疇昔已居宸極，群望所屬。

translations.literal: Liu Youqiu spoke to Prince of Song Chengqi and Prince of Ping Longji, saying: "The Prince of Xiang long ago already occupied the imperial throne; the hopes of the multitude belong to him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Youqiu urged Prince of Song Chengqi and Prince of Ping Longji: "Our father once held the throne himself, and all eyes are on him again.

sentences.zh: 今人心未安，家國事重，相王豈得尚守小節，不早即位以鎭天下乎！」

translations.literal: Now people's hearts are not yet settled; state and family affairs are weighty—how can the Prince of Xiang still cling to small proprieties and not early accede to the throne to stabilize the realm!"
translations.idiomatic: The people are still unsettled and the dynasty hangs in the balance—can he really keep clinging to modesty and refuse to take the throne and steady the realm!"

sentences.zh: 隆基曰：「王性恬淡，不以代事嬰懷。

translations.literal: Longji said: "The Prince's nature is tranquil and detached; he does not brood over matters of succession.
translations.idiomatic: Longji replied: "Father is by nature quiet and unambitious; the throne does not weigh on his mind.

sentences.zh: 雖有天下，猶讓於人，況親兄之子，安肯代之乎！」

translations.literal: Though he had the realm, he still yielded it to another—how much less would he be willing to replace his elder brother's own son!"
translations.idiomatic: Even when he already held the empire he yielded it to another—how could he now supplant his own brother's son!"

sentences.zh: 幽求曰：「衆心不可違，王雖欲髙居獨善，其如社稷何！」

translations.literal: Youqiu said: "The multitude's hearts cannot be defied; though the Prince wishes to dwell aloft in solitary virtue, what of the altar of state!"
translations.idiomatic: Youqiu pressed on: "The people's will cannot be ignored. However much he wishes to stand apart, what will become of the dynasty!"

sentences.zh: 成器、隆基入見相王，極言其事，相王乃許之。

translations.literal: Chengqi and Longji entered to see the Prince of Xiang and spoke urgently of the matter; the Prince of Xiang then consented.
translations.idiomatic: Chengqi and Longji went in together and pleaded at length until the Prince of Xiang at last agreed.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，少帝在太極殿東隅西向，相王立於梓宮旁，太平公主曰：「皇帝欲以此位讓叔父，可乎？」

translations.literal: On jiachen, the Lesser Emperor was in the eastern corner of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate facing west; the Prince of Xiang stood beside the coffin of the late emperor. Princess Taiping said: "The emperor wishes to yield this throne to his uncle—is it acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen the young emperor sat in the eastern corner of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate facing west, while the Prince of Xiang stood beside the late emperor's coffin. Princess Taiping asked: "His Majesty wishes to yield the throne to his uncle—is that acceptable?"

sentences.zh: 幽求跪曰：「國家多難，皇帝仁孝，追蹤堯、舜，誠合至公；

translations.literal: Youqiu knelt and said: "The state has many hardships; the emperor is benevolent and filial, following in the footsteps of Yao and Shun—this truly accords with supreme fairness;
translations.idiomatic: Youqiu knelt and answered: "The realm has suffered one crisis after another. In yielding the throne out of filial duty, His Majesty follows the example of Yao and Shun and acts with perfect fairness;

sentences.zh: 相王代之任重，慈愛尤厚矣。」
