translations.literal: the Prince of Xiang in replacing him bears a heavy charge, and his kindness is especially deep."
translations.idiomatic: for the Prince of Xiang to take his place is a weighty burden, yet his affection for the boy is all the deeper."

sentences.zh: 乃以少帝制傳位相王。

translations.literal: Thereupon by the Lesser Emperor's edict the throne was transferred to the Prince of Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then issued in the young emperor's name transferring the throne to the Prince of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 時少帝猶在御座，太平公主進曰：「天下之心已歸相王，此非兒座！」

translations.literal: At that time the Lesser Emperor was still on the imperial seat. Princess Taiping stepped forward and said: "The hearts of the realm already belong to the Prince of Xiang—this is no seat for a child!"
translations.idiomatic: The young emperor was still on the throne when Princess Taiping stepped forward: "All hearts already belong to the Prince of Xiang—this is no seat for a child!"

sentences.zh: 遂提下之。

translations.literal: Thereupon she pulled him down from it.
translations.idiomatic: She then pulled him from the throne.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，御承天門，赦天下。

translations.literal: Ruizong acceded; he took the throne at Chengtian Gate and proclaimed a general amnesty throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Ruizong took the throne, appeared at Chengtian Gate, and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 復以少帝爲温王。

translations.literal: The Lesser Emperor was again made Prince of Wen.
translations.idiomatic: The young emperor was again enfeoffed as Prince of Wen.

sentences.zh: 以鐘紹京爲中書令。

translations.literal: Zhong Shaojing was made Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Shaojing was appointed Secretariat Director.

sentences.zh: 鐘紹京少爲司農録事，既典朝政，縱情賞罰，衆皆惡之。

translations.literal: Zhong Shaojing in youth had been a clerk in the Ministry of Revenue; once he held the reins of court government, he indulged rewards and punishments at will, and all hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Shaojing had begun his career as a low clerk in the Ministry of Revenue; once he controlled the government he handed out rewards and punishments as he pleased, and everyone despised him.

sentences.zh: 太常少卿薛稷勸其上表禮讓，紹京從之。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Xue Ji urged him to submit a memorial declining on grounds of propriety; Shaojing followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ji, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, urged him to submit a memorial of polite refusal, and Shaojing agreed.

sentences.zh: 稷入言於上曰：「紹京雖有勳勞，素無才德，出自胥徒，一旦超居元宰，恐失聖朝具瞻之美。」

translations.literal: Ji entered and spoke to the emperor, saying: "Although Shaojing has meritorious service, he has never had talent or virtue; he came from clerk and runner ranks, and in one morning leaped to the highest ministerial post—I fear this will lose the beauty of the holy court as object of universal regard."
translations.idiomatic: Ji went in and told the emperor: "Shaojing may have earned merit in the coup, but he has never shown talent or character. A clerk risen overnight to chief minister will tarnish the dignity our dynasty expects of its highest office."

sentences.zh: 上以爲然。

translations.literal: The emperor thought this correct.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 丙午，改除戸部尚書，尋出爲蜀州刺史。

translations.literal: On bingwu he was transferred to Minister of the Household; soon afterward he was sent out as Prefect of Shu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu he was reassigned as Minister of the Household and soon afterward dispatched as prefect of Shu.

sentences.zh: 上將立太子，以宋王成器嫡長，而平王隆基有大功，疑不能決。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to install a crown prince. Prince of Song Chengqi was the eldest legitimate son, yet Prince of Ping Longji had great merit—the emperor hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor came to choose an heir, Prince of Song Chengqi was the eldest legitimate son, but Prince of Ping Longji had saved the dynasty, and he could not make up his mind.

sentences.zh: 成器辭曰：「國家安則先嫡長，國家危則先有功；

translations.literal: Chengqi declined, saying: "When the state is secure, precedence goes to the eldest legitimate son; when the state is in peril, precedence goes to the one with merit;
translations.idiomatic: Chengqi declined, saying: "When the realm is secure, the eldest legitimate son comes first; when it is in peril, merit comes first;

sentences.zh: 苟違其宜，四海失望。

translations.literal: if this propriety is violated, the four seas will lose hope.
translations.idiomatic: to choose wrongly would disappoint the whole empire.

sentences.zh: 臣死不敢居平王之上。」

translations.literal: Your servant would die rather than stand above the Prince of Ping."
translations.idiomatic: I would rather die than rank above Prince of Ping."

sentences.zh: 涕泣固請者累日。

translations.literal: Weeping, he firmly petitioned for many days.
translations.idiomatic: For days he wept and pleaded until the emperor relented.

sentences.zh: 大臣亦多言平王功大宜立。

translations.literal: The great ministers also mostly said the Prince of Ping's merit was great and he ought to be installed.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers likewise argued that Longji's service warranted the succession.

sentences.zh: 劉幽求曰：「臣聞除天下之禍者，當享天下之福。

translations.literal: Liu Youqiu said: "Your servant has heard that one who removes calamity from the realm ought to enjoy the realm's blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Youqiu said: "I have always heard that whoever lifts a curse from the realm deserves its blessing.

sentences.zh: 平王拯社稷之危，求君親之難，論功莫大，語德最賢，無可疑者。」

translations.literal: The Prince of Ping rescued the altar of state from peril and sought out difficulty for ruler and father—in merit none greater, in virtue most worthy; there is nothing doubtful."
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Ping rescued the dynasty at its darkest hour and risked his life for emperor and father alike. In merit none surpasses him; in virtue none excels him. There can be no question."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted the argument.

sentences.zh: 丁未，立平王隆基爲太子。

translations.literal: On dingwei Prince of Ping Longji was installed as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei Prince of Ping Longji was named crown prince.

sentences.zh: 隆基復表讓成器，不許。

translations.literal: Longji again submitted a memorial yielding to Chengqi; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Longji again petitioned to yield the place to Chengqi, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 則天大聖皇后復舊號爲天後。

translations.literal: Empress Wu Zetian the Great Sage Holy Empress restored her old title as Empress Tian.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu Zetian the Great Sage Holy Empress was restored to her former title of Empress Tian.

sentences.zh: 追謚雍王賢曰章懷太子。

translations.literal: Prince of Yong Xian was posthumously titled Crown Prince Zhanghuai.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yong Xian was posthumously honored as Crown Prince Zhanghuai.

sentences.zh: 戊申，以宋王成器爲雍州牧、揚州大都督、太子太師。

translations.literal: On wushen Prince of Song Chengqi was made Governor of Yong Prefecture, Great Commander of Yangzhou, and Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen Prince of Song Chengqi was appointed Governor of Yong, Great Commander of Yangzhou, and Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 置温王重茂於内宅。

translations.literal: Prince of Wen Chongmao was housed in the inner residence.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wen Chongmao was lodged in the inner palace quarters.

sentences.zh: 以太常少卿薛稷爲黃門侍郎，參知機務。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Xue Ji was made Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, participating in handling state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ji, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was made Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and joined in managing state affairs.

sentences.zh: 稷以工書，事上於籓邸，其子伯陽尚仙源公主，故爲相。

translations.literal: Ji, for skill in calligraphy, had served the emperor when he was at his princely residence; his son Boyang had married Princess Xianyuan—therefore he became chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Ji had served the emperor at his princely residence through his skill in calligraphy, and his son Boyang had married Princess Xianyuan—connections that now made him a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 追削武三思、武崇訓爵謚，斫棺暴屍，平其墳墓。

translations.literal: Posthumously stripped Wu Sansi and Wu Chongxun of titles and posthumous names; their coffins were chopped open and corpses exposed; their tombs were leveled.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sansi and Wu Chongxun were posthumously stripped of rank and posthumous honors; their coffins were broken open, their corpses exposed, and their tombs razed.

sentences.zh: 以許州刺史姚元之爲兵部尚書、同中書門下三品，宋州刺史韋嗣立、許州刺史蕭至忠爲中書令，絳州刺史趙彦昭爲中書侍郎，華州刺史崔湜爲吏部侍郎，並同平章事。

translations.literal: Prefect of Xu Prefecture Yao Yuanzhi was made Minister of War and Fellow of the Third Rank; Prefect of Song Prefecture Wei Sili and Prefect of Xu Prefecture Xiao Zhizhong were made Secretariat Directors; Prefect of Jiang Prefecture Zhao Yanzhao Vice Director of the Secretariat; Prefect of Hua Prefecture Cui Shi Vice Minister of Personnel—all as Chief Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yuanzhi, prefect of Xu, was made Minister of War and Fellow of the Third Rank; Wei Sili, prefect of Song, and Xiao Zhizhong, prefect of Xu, were appointed Secretariat Directors; Zhao Yanzhao, prefect of Jiang, Vice Director of the Secretariat; and Cui Shi, prefect of Hua, Vice Minister of Personnel—all as chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 越州長史宋之問，饒州刺史冉祖雍，坐諂附韋、武，皆流嶺表。

translations.literal: Song Zhiwen, prefectural secretary of Yue Prefecture, and Ran Zuyong, prefect of Rao Prefecture, for fawning attachment to the Wei and Wu factions, were both exiled beyond the Ling mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Song Zhiwen, prefectural secretary of Yue, and Ran Zuyong, prefect of Rao, for having fawned on the Wei and Wu factions, were both exiled beyond the Ling range.

sentences.zh: 己酉，立衡陽王成義爲申王，巴陵王隆范爲岐王，彭城王隆業爲薛王；

translations.literal: On jiyou Prince of Hengyang Chengyi was installed as Prince of Shen, Prince of Baling Longfan as Prince of Qi, and Prince of Pengcheng Longye as Prince of Xue;
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou Prince of Hengyang Chengyi was enfeoffed as Prince of Shen, Prince of Baling Longfan as Prince of Qi, and Prince of Pengcheng Longye as Prince of Xue;

sentences.zh: 加太平公主實封滿萬戸。

translations.literal: Princess Taiping's actual fief was increased to a full ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Taiping's personal fief was raised to the full ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 太平公主沈敏多權略，武後以爲類己，故於諸子中獨愛幸，頗得預密謀，然尚畏武後之嚴，未敢招權勢；

translations.literal: Princess Taiping was deep, keen, and rich in stratagem. Empress Wu thought her like herself, and therefore among all her children loved and favored her alone; she was allowed to take part in secret counsels, yet still feared Empress Wu's severity and did not dare gather power and influence;
translations.idiomatic: Princess Taiping was shrewd, quick, and skilled in intrigue. Empress Wu saw herself in her and favored her above all her children, admitting her to secret counsel; yet she still feared the empress's severity and did not dare openly amass power;

sentences.zh: 及誅張易之，公主有力焉。

translations.literal: when Zhang Yizhi was executed, the princess had force in the matter.
translations.idiomatic: and when Zhang Yizhi was killed, she had played a decisive part.

sentences.zh: 中宗之世，韋後、安樂公主皆畏之，又與太子共誅韋氏。

translations.literal: In Emperor Zhongzong's reign, Empress Wei and Princess Anle both feared her; she also joined the crown prince in executing the Wei clan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhongzong, Empress Wei and Princess Anle both feared her, and she later joined the crown prince in overthrowing the Wei faction.

sentences.zh: 既屢立大功，益尊重，上常與之圖議大政，毎入奏事，坐語移時；

translations.literal: Having repeatedly achieved great merit, she grew ever more honored. The emperor often deliberated on great affairs with her; each time she entered to report business, they would sit and talk for a long while;
translations.idiomatic: After repeated triumphs her standing only rose. The emperor often consulted her on major policy, and when she came to discuss affairs they would talk for hours;

sentences.zh: 或時不朝謁，則宰相就第咨之。

translations.literal: sometimes when she did not attend court audience, the chief ministers would go to her residence to consult her.
translations.idiomatic: if she skipped court, the chief ministers would visit her house for guidance.

sentences.zh: 毎宰相奏事，上輒問：「嘗與太平議否？」

translations.literal: Each time a chief minister reported business, the emperor would ask: "Have you already discussed this with Taiping?"
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a chief minister reported business, the emperor would ask: "Have you discussed this with Taiping?"

sentences.zh: 又問：「與三郎議否？」

translations.literal: He would also ask: "Have you discussed it with Third Son?"
translations.idiomatic: Then: "And with Third Son?"

sentences.zh: 然後可之。

translations.literal: Only then would he approve it.
translations.idiomatic: Only after both questions were answered would he approve.

sentences.zh: 三郎，謂太子也。

translations.literal: Third Son meant the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: "Third Son" was his nickname for the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 公主所欲，上無不聽，自宰相以下，進退系其一言，其餘薦士驟歴淸顯者不可勝數，權傾人主，趨附其門者如市。

translations.literal: Whatever the princess desired, the emperor never refused to listen; from chief ministers downward, advancement and dismissal hung on a single word from her. Besides this, recommended men who suddenly passed through clear and eminent posts were beyond counting; her power tilted past the sovereign's, and those rushing to attach to her gate were like a market.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever she wanted, the emperor granted; from chief ministers down, careers rose or fell on her word. The men she recommended into high office were beyond counting. Her power overshadowed the throne itself, and suitors packed her gate like a marketplace.

sentences.zh: 子薛崇行、崇敏、崇簡皆封王，田園遍於近甸，收市營遠諸器玩，遠至嶺、蜀，輸送者相屬於路，居處奉養，擬於宮掖。

translations.literal: Her sons Xue Chongxing, Chongmin, and Chongjian were all enfeoffed as princes; fields and gardens spread throughout the near suburbs; she collected and bought distant curios and playthings from as far as the Ling mountains and Shu; carriers on the roads followed one after another; her dwelling and upkeep rivaled the palace inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Her sons Xue Chongxing, Chongmin, and Chongjian were all made princes. Her estates filled the capital suburbs; she hoarded rare treasures from as far as Lingnan and Shu, with convoys crowding the roads. Her household lived in a style that rivaled the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 追贈郎岌、燕欽融諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Lang Ba and Yan Qinrong were posthumously made Remonstrance Grand Masters.
translations.idiomatic: Lang Ba and Yan Qinrong were posthumously honored as Remonstrance Grand Masters.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，庚戌朔，贈韋月將宣州刺史。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, first day gengxu: Wei Yuejiang was posthumously made Prefect of Xuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, on the first day, gengxu, Wei Yuejiang was posthumously honored as prefect of Xuan.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，以兵部侍郎崔日用爲黃門侍郎，參知機務。

translations.literal: On guichou Vice Minister of War Cui Riyong was made Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, participating in handling state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou Cui Riyong, Vice Minister of War, was made Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and joined in managing state affairs.

sentences.zh: 追復故太子重俊位號；

translations.literal: The former crown prince Chongjun's rank and title were posthumously restored;
translations.idiomatic: The late crown prince Chongjun's rank and title were posthumously restored;

sentences.zh: 雪敬暉、桓彦范、崔玄□、張柬之、袁恕己、成王行裡、李多祚等罪，復其官爵。

translations.literal: The crimes of Jing Hui, Huan Yanfan, Cui Xuan□, Zhang Jianzhi, Yuan Shuji, Prince of Cheng Xingli, Li Duozuo, and others were cleared; their offices and titles were restored.
translations.idiomatic: the convictions of Jing Hui, Huan Yanfan, Cui Xuanwei, Zhang Jianzhi, Yuan Shuji, Prince of Cheng Xingli, Li Duozuo, and others were overturned and their offices and titles restored.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，以洛州長史宋璟檢校吏部尚書、同中書門下三品；

translations.literal: On dingsi Prefectural Secretary of Luo Prefecture Song Jing was made acting Minister of Personnel and Fellow of the Third Rank;
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi Song Jing, prefectural secretary of Luo, was made acting Minister of Personnel and Fellow of the Third Rank;

sentences.zh: 岑羲罷爲右散騎常侍，兼刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Cen Xi was removed and made Right Regular Attendant, concurrently Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Xi was dismissed as chief minister and made Right Regular Attendant, concurrently Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 璟與姚元之協心革中宗弊政，進忠良，退不肖，賞罰盡公，請托不行，納紀修舉，當時翕然以爲復有貞觀、永徽之風。

translations.literal: Song Jing and Yao Yuanzhi with one heart reformed the corrupt policies of Emperor Zhongzong's reign: advancing the loyal and good, removing the unworthy, making rewards and punishments wholly fair, refusing patronage requests, receiving remonstrance and restoring discipline—at the time all harmoniously thought the Zhenguan and Yonghui airs had returned.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing and Yao Yuanzhi worked in concert to purge the abuses of Zhongzong's reign: promoting the worthy, removing the corrupt, judging without favor, refusing private petitions, and restoring discipline. Many believed the upright spirit of the Zhenguan and Yonghui eras had returned.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，崔湜罷爲尚書左丞，張錫爲絳州刺史，蕭至忠爲晉州刺史，韋嗣立爲許州刺史，趙彦昭爲宋州刺史。

translations.literal: On renxu Cui Shi was removed and made Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat; Zhang Xi was made Prefect of Jiang Prefecture; Xiao Zhizhong Prefect of Jin Prefecture; Wei Sili Prefect of Xu Prefecture; Zhao Yanzhao Prefect of Song Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu Cui Shi was demoted to Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat; Zhang Xi was sent to Jiang as prefect; Xiao Zhizhong to Jin; Wei Sili to Xu; and Zhao Yanzhao to Song.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，姚元之兼中書令，兵部尚書、同中書門下三品李嶠貶懷州刺史。

translations.literal: On bingyin Yao Yuanzhi additionally held the post of Secretariat Director; Minister of War and Fellow of the Third Rank Li Qiao was demoted to Prefect of Huai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin Yao Yuanzhi was also made Secretariat Director, while Li Qiao, Minister of War and Fellow of the Third Rank, was demoted to prefect of Huai.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，太子少師、同中書門下三品唐休璟致仕，右武衞大將軍、同中書門下三品張仁願罷爲左衞大將軍。

translations.literal: On dingmao Tang Xiujing, Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and Fellow of the Third Rank, retired from office; Zhang Renyuan, General of the Right Martial Guard and Fellow of the Third Rank, was removed and made General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao Tang Xiujing, Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and Fellow of the Third Rank, retired; Zhang Renyuan, General of the Right Martial Guard and Fellow of the Third Rank, was relieved and made General of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎、參知機務崔日用與中書侍郎、參知機務薛稷爭於上前，稷曰：「日用傾側，向附武三思，非忠臣；

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and participant in state affairs Cui Riyong and Vice Director of the Secretariat and participant in state affairs Xue Ji quarreled before the emperor. Ji said: "Riyong is shifting and crooked; he formerly attached himself to Wu Sansi—not a loyal minister;
translations.idiomatic: Cui Riyong and Xue Ji, both vice directors participating in state affairs, quarreled before the emperor. Ji accused him: "Riyong is a trimmer who once clung to Wu Sansi—no loyal minister;

sentences.zh: 賣友邀功，非義士。」

translations.literal: he sold friends to claim merit—not a man of righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: he betrayed friends to claim credit—no man of honor."

sentences.zh: 日用曰：「臣往雖有過，今立大功。

translations.literal: Riyong said: "Your servant though once had faults, now has achieved great merit.
translations.idiomatic: Riyong retorted: "I may once have erred, but I have now rendered great service.

sentences.zh: 稷外托國姻，内附張易之、宗楚客，非傾側而何！」

translations.literal: Ji outwardly relied on imperial marriage ties, inwardly attached to Zhang Yizhi and Zong Chuke—if not shifting and crooked, then what!"
translations.idiomatic: Ji hides behind imperial marriage while serving Zhang Yizhi and Zong Chuke at heart—what is that if not trimming!"

sentences.zh: 上由是兩罷之，戊辰，以日用爲雍州長史，稷爲左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore dismissed both. On wuchen Riyong was made Prefectural Secretary of Yong Prefecture, and Ji Left Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dismissed them both. On wuchen Riyong was made prefectural secretary of Yong, and Ji Left Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 己巳，赦天下，改元；

translations.literal: On jisi a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm and the era name was changed;
translations.idiomatic: On jisi the emperor proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name;

sentences.zh: 凡韋氏餘黨未施行者，鹹赦之。

translations.literal: all remaining Wei faction members whose punishments had not yet been carried out were entirely pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: all remaining members of the Wei faction whose sentences had not yet been executed were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，廢武氏崇恩廟及昊陵、順陵，追廢韋後爲庶人，安樂公主爲悖逆庶人。

translations.literal: On yihai the Wu clan's Temple of Grateful Succession and the Hao and Shun Mausoleums were abolished; Empress Wei was posthumously demoted to commoner status and Princess Anle to Rebellious Commoner.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai the Wu clan's Temple of Grateful Succession and the Hao and Shun imperial tombs were abolished; Empress Wei was posthumously reduced to commoner rank and Princess Anle to Rebellious Commoner.

sentences.zh: 韋後之臨朝也，吏部侍郎鄭愔貶江州司馬，潛過均州，與刺史譙王重福及洛陽人張靈均謀舉兵誅韋氏，未發而韋氏敗。

translations.literal: When Empress Wei held court, Vice Minister of Personnel Zheng Yin was demoted to Military Adjutant of Jiang Prefecture; secretly passing through Jun Prefecture, he joined Prefect Prince of Qiao Zhongfu and Luoyang man Zhang Lingjun in plotting to raise troops and execute the Wei clan—before they acted, the Wei faction fell.
translations.idiomatic: While Empress Wei held power, Zheng Yin, Vice Minister of Personnel, was demoted to adjutant of Jiang. Passing secretly through Jun Prefecture, he joined Prince of Qiao Zhongfu, the prefect, and Zhang Lingjun of Luoyang in a plot to raise troops and destroy the Wei faction—but before they moved, the Wei clan had already fallen.

sentences.zh: 重福遷集州刺史，未行，靈均説重福曰：「大王地居嫡長，當爲天子。

translations.literal: Zhongfu was transferred to Prefect of Ji Prefecture; before he departed, Lingjun persuaded Zhongfu, saying: "Great Prince, by position you are the eldest legitimate son—you ought to be Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfu was reassigned as prefect of Ji but had not yet left when Lingjun urged him: "Your Highness stands first among the legitimate sons—you should be emperor.

sentences.zh: 相王雖有功，不當繼統。

translations.literal: Though the Prince of Xiang has merit, he ought not to succeed to the line.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xiang may have merit, but he has no right to the succession.

sentences.zh: 東都士庶，皆願王來。

translations.literal: The gentry and commoners of the Eastern Capital all wish Your Highness to come.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the Eastern Capital all long for Your Highness to come.

sentences.zh: 王若潛入洛陽，發左右屯營兵，襲殺留守。

translations.literal: If Your Highness secretly enters Luoyang, rouses the Left and Right Garrison Camp troops, and strikes and kills the resident commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Highness slips into Luoyang, mobilize the Left and Right Garrison troops, and strike down the resident commissioner.

sentences.zh: 據東都，如從天而下也。

translations.literal: holding the Eastern Capital would be like descending from Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: once you hold the Eastern Capital, victory will fall upon you like heaven's decree.

sentences.zh: 然後西取陝州，東取河南北，天下指麾可定。」

translations.literal: Then west take Shan Prefecture, east take Henan North Circuit—the realm could be settled at a gesture."
translations.idiomatic: Then seize Shan to the west and Henan North to the east, and the empire will be yours at a wave of the hand."

sentences.zh: 重福從之。

translations.literal: Zhongfu followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfu agreed.

sentences.zh: 靈均乃密與愔結謀，聚徒數十人。

translations.literal: Lingjun then secretly joined with Yin in forming a plot and gathered several dozen followers.
translations.idiomatic: Lingjun then secretly allied with Yin and mustered several dozen men.

sentences.zh: 時愔自秘書少監左遷沅州刺史，遲留洛陽以俟重福，爲重福草制，立重福爲帝，改元爲中元克復。

translations.literal: At the time Yin had been demoted from Vice Director of the Secretariat to Prefect of Yuan Prefecture; he delayed in Luoyang waiting for Zhongfu, and drafted for Zhongfu an edict installing him as emperor and changing the era name to Zhongyuan Restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Yin had been demoted from Vice Director of the Secretariat to prefect of Yuan but lingered in Luoyang awaiting Zhongfu. He drafted an enthronement edict for Zhongfu and a new era name, Zhongyuan Restoration.

sentences.zh: 尊上爲皇季叔，以温王爲皇太弟，愔爲左丞相知内外文部尚書知吏部事。

translations.literal: The emperor was to be honored as Imperial Junior Uncle; Prince of Wen was made Grand Younger Brother of the Emperor; Yin was made Left Chief Minister, concurrently managing the Ministries of Civil Affairs and Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: The edict honored the emperor as Imperial Junior Uncle, made Prince of Wen Grand Younger Brother of the Emperor, and appointed Yin Left Chief Minister with charge of both civil and personnel affairs.

sentences.zh: 重福與靈均詐乘驛詣東都，愔先供張駙馬都尉裴巽第以待重福。

translations.literal: Zhongfu and Lingjun falsely claimed relay credentials to travel to the Eastern Capital; Yin first prepared the residence of Commandant of Cavalry Pei Xun to await Zhongfu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfu and Lingjun traveled to the Eastern Capital under false relay credentials while Yin prepared the mansion of Commandant of Cavalry Pei Xun to receive Zhongfu.

sentences.zh: 洛陽縣官微聞其謀。

translations.literal: The Luoyang county clerk faintly heard of their plot.
translations.idiomatic: A clerk in Luoyang county caught wind of the conspiracy.
